RM-P1-005.explanation: The father's grave voice becomes Rin's somber reply. This replaces the remembered contrast between his gravity and her dutiful behavior.

RM-P1-005.sourceReading: Rin answers her father's grave voice with a properly behaved “yes.”

RM-P1-008.explanation: The English expands a judgment about the world of mages into a judgment about the entire world.

RM-R5C-F001.sourceReading: The source explicitly describes the entire portion of the left arm beyond the elbow as a bucket-like opening.
RM-R5C-F001.explanation: The Japanese specifies the extent and shape of the damage beyond Shirou’s elbow. “A wound this big” leaves those concrete features unspecified.

RM-R5E-F004.explanation: The English changes the uniform's hem into a sleeve.

RM-R12A-F020.explanation: Future treatment of the captive is rendered as treatment that has already happened.

RM-S07I-F004.explanation: “I’ve forbid” uses the infinitive where the past participle “forbidden” is required.
RM-S07I-F004.sourceReading: The narration refers to what Shirou has forbidden himself to consider.

RM-S09C-F007.explanation: The English turns a claim about winning the coming rematch into a counterfactual about losing the previous fight.
RM-S09C-F007.sourceReading: 今だって concerns the present situation and the upcoming encounter: Shinji says he cannot lose as long as Saber stays out of it.

RM-S0312-F020.sourceReading: The Tohsaka comparison kindles a negative feeling so slight the visitor does not notice it. The Japanese does not identify that feeling as disappointment.

RM-S0507-F006.explanation: The English drops Saturday from the stated two-day time reference.
RM-S0507-F006.sourceReading: 二日前の土曜日 specifies both two days earlier and the day of the week.

RM-S0507-F009.explanation: The English turns a risk of weakening to death into a certain outcome.
RM-S0507-F009.sourceReading: 衰弱死しかねない means that they could weaken and die, rather than that they inevitably will.

RM-S0507-F010.explanation: The English removes the condition that either the Master or Servant choose to activate the effect.
RM-S0507-F010.sourceReading: どちらかがその気になれば makes the result conditional on either of them choosing to act.

RM-S0508X-F006.sourceReading: 十中八九 expresses near certainty—eight or nine times out of ten—while だろう retains the inference.

RM-S1303B-F018.sourceReading: Even if Saber was stronger than Caster expected, Rin doubts that an unprepared assault would succeed.

RM-S1303B-F019.sourceReading: だけは restricts the exception to this sword.

RM-S0406B-F007.explanation: The English changes an instruction about Shirou's role as Master into an instruction to stay behind Saber.

RM-RIN-003.explanation: The English combines Rin's pressure with Shirou's recollection. It drops his correction that remembering that night, rather than simply facing her outburst, explains why he freezes.
RM-RIN-003.description: The English combines Rin's pressure with Shirou's recollection. It drops his correction that remembering that night, rather than simply facing her outburst, explains why he freezes.
RM-RIN-003.sourceReading: Shirou describes being overawed by Rin's sudden outburst, then revises that explanation: remembering that night makes him freeze.

RM-R2-012.explanation: The Japanese describes dozens of exchanges of offense and defense. “Many attacks” loses the numerical scale and the defensive half of the exchange.

RM-R14N-F007.explanation: Lancer's question about the point of getting serious in this particular exchange becomes a general question about serious battle. His subsequent reasoning survives, but its opening distinction is blurred.
RM-R14N-F007.description: Lancer's question about the point of getting serious in this particular exchange becomes a general question about serious battle. His subsequent reasoning survives, but its opening distinction is blurred.
RM-R14N-F007.sourceReading: Lancer asks what getting serious in this kind of combat would accomplish, before distinguishing ordinary exchanges from using a fatal Noble Phantasm.

RM-R10E-F004.explanation: Rin describes the house as unusually natural and open for a mage’s workshop. “Naturalistic” describes imitation of nature, changing the word’s sense in this household contrast.

RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F013.explanation: Saber explains that mages with little inherited history use things with an established form as magical power. The English makes those things merely a means “to use magical energy,” losing their role as the power resource.

RM-S0411B-F016.explanation: “I can could” duplicates incompatible modals. Later, plural “weapons” becomes singular “it.” Both constructions obscure otherwise straightforward clauses.

RM-HF-D4-KIREI-F012.explanation: The pronoun case is nonstandard, but Kotomine's comparison with Kiritsugu remains intact. This belongs in a language-editing discussion rather than this character dossier.
RM-HF-D4-KIREI-F012.description: The pronoun case is nonstandard, but Kotomine's comparison with Kiritsugu remains intact. This belongs in a language-editing discussion rather than this character dossier.
RM-HF-D4-KIREI-F012.sourceReading: Others equated Kotomine with Kiritsugu on a different basis from the humanity Shirou has just described.

RM-S15C-F003.explanation: The Japanese reaffirms that demons definitely exist. The English instead describes how tenaciously some demons corrupt people.
RM-S15C-F003.sourceReading: The sentence reiterates the definite existence of demons before describing their corruption of people and the earth.

RM-R10B-F006.explanation: Shirou says Rin’s remark irritates him. “Gets my gall” mixes English expressions for irritation without producing the intended idiom.

RM-R04K-F009.explanation: Archer says Rin cannot be satisfied without picking a fight. “Can’t stand without starting a fight” loses what she cannot stand or what would satisfy her.

RM-R2-009.explanation: The Japanese describes his belittling of himself. “Humility” recasts that self-deprecation as modesty.

RM-R2-019.explanation: The singular subject “the only thing” takes “remain” where it requires “remains.”

RM-P3-C010.description: Rin’s prediction that Archer will die remains framed as her premonition.
RM-P3-C010.explanation: The English keeps Rin’s prediction inside her explicitly named premonition, before the attack is resolved.
RM-P3-C010.sourceReading: Rin does not know what Lancer’s Noble Phantasm is, but has an unprecedented intuition that Archer will die if it is unleashed.

RM-S09G-F023.explanation: Shirou pulls Rider’s arm to reverse their positions. The English instead has him pull himself up using her arms; it keeps the reversed positions but changes the movement that produces them.

RM-R7C-006.explanation: The English retains “I can’t say for sure,” then declares “I’m positive.” The Japanese consistently presents the first-floor location as what Rin senses without being able to state it definitively.

RM-S1408B-F011.explanation: The Japanese describes words and emotional damage as beyond repair. “Dangerous” and “really hurt” retain seriousness but omit that irreversibility.

RM-S1512B-C004.description: The red light and unusually bright nighttime setting are both retained.
RM-S1512B-C004.explanation: The English preserves both the red phosphorescence moving in the wind and the setting’s excessive brightness for nighttime.
RM-S1512B-C004.sourceReading: Red phosphorescence moves in the wind, and the precinct is unusually bright for night.

RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F005.description: The English substitutes a sense of Saber's reality for explicit awareness of her as a woman. The surrounding attraction remains, and this belongs in a dossier about Shirou's perception.
RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F005.explanation: The English substitutes a sense of Saber's reality for explicit awareness of her as a woman. The surrounding attraction remains, and this belongs in a dossier about Shirou's perception.
RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F005.sourceReading: The everyday reality of Saber's clothes makes Shirou involuntarily conscious of her as a woman.

RM-P1-025.description: Ayako's praise of a lovely romantic possibility becomes a description of it as a tall tale. She need not believe Rin in the Japanese, but her response does not itself dismiss the story as far-fetched.
RM-P1-025.explanation: Ayako's praise of a lovely romantic possibility becomes a description of it as a tall tale. She need not believe Rin in the Japanese, but her response does not itself dismiss the story as far-fetched.
RM-P1-025.sourceReading: Ayako appreciates the proposed explanation as a lovely romantic story, without mocking Rin or necessarily believing it is true.

RM-SEPI-F018.description: Rin's difficulty opening a sensitive conversation becomes difficulty making small talk. Her ensuing question about Sakura's adjustment shows what she is preparing to discuss.
RM-SEPI-F018.explanation: Rin's difficulty opening a sensitive conversation becomes difficulty making small talk. Her ensuing question about Sakura's adjustment shows what she is preparing to discuss.
RM-SEPI-F018.sourceReading: Left alone with Sakura, Rin finds it awkward to open the conversation she needs to have.

RM-HF-D10A-F002.description: Shirou's acceptance of his wandering attention becomes an effort not to be flustered. The change concerns his handling of attraction.
RM-HF-D10A-F002.explanation: Shirou's acceptance of his wandering attention becomes an effort not to be flustered. The change concerns his handling of attraction.
RM-HF-D10A-F002.sourceReading: Shirou accepts his involuntary attention to Sakura and will not make excuses for it.

RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F013.description: The English leaves the ongoing scope of Shirou's thanks implicit. It does not say he appreciates only this dinner.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F013.explanation: The English leaves the ongoing scope of Shirou's thanks implicit. It does not say he appreciates only this dinner.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F013.sourceReading: Shirou explicitly thanks Sakura for her ongoing help after praising dinner.

RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F004.description: Shirou calls his intended actions unreasonable or reckless; the English instead calls his ideals silly. This changes the target of his self-deprecation without proving that he rejects those ideals.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F004.explanation: Shirou calls his intended actions unreasonable or reckless; the English instead calls his ideals silly. This changes the target of his self-deprecation without proving that he rejects those ideals.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F004.sourceReading: Shirou needs enough physical ability to carry out his own unreasonable or reckless undertakings as he pictures them.

RM-R04G-F003.description: The tour remains funny, but Shirou's ceremonious guide voice becomes casual description. This reduces the contrast between his authoritative delivery and unreliable information.
RM-R04G-F003.explanation: The tour remains funny, but Shirou's ceremonious guide voice becomes casual description. This reduces the contrast between his authoritative delivery and unreliable information.
RM-R04G-F003.sourceReading: Shirou presents dubious measurements and land-use commentary in conspicuously formal guide language.

RM-HF-D10E-F002.description: Rin's sarcasm about Shirou's attentiveness becomes a direct accusation that he is childish.
RM-HF-D10E-F002.explanation: Rin's sarcasm about Shirou's attentiveness becomes a direct accusation that he is childish.
RM-HF-D10E-F002.sourceReading: Rin sarcastically remarks on the trouble Shirou takes to please Illya.

RM-R04K-F003.description: Rin's dismissal of Archer's commentary becomes the gendered rebuke “mansplaining.” Their discussion concerns men and women, but the Japanese interruption does not characterize his explanation in those terms.
RM-R04K-F003.explanation: Rin's dismissal of Archer's commentary becomes the gendered rebuke “mansplaining.” Their discussion concerns men and women, but the Japanese interruption does not characterize his explanation in those terms.
RM-R04K-F003.sourceReading: Rin cuts off Archer's commentary and tells him to help open the windows.

RM-P1-021.description: The English explicitly names romance before the later explanation of the boyfriend contest. The Japanese allows that inference while keeping the exchange's subject unstated.
RM-P1-021.explanation: The English explicitly names romance before the later explanation of the boyfriend contest. The Japanese allows that inference while keeping the exchange's subject unstated.
RM-P1-021.sourceReading: Rin says neither woman can afford to take her time, without explicitly naming romance. The supplied page74 later identifies their boyfriend contest.

RM-R04D-F012.description: English preserves the turn from apparent accident warning to Taiga's threat. It drops her little snapping demonstration and moves the self-reveal away from the sentence's final beat.
RM-R04D-F012.explanation: English preserves the turn from apparent accident warning to Taiga's threat. It drops her little snapping demonstration and moves the self-reveal away from the sentence's final beat.
RM-R04D-F012.sourceReading: An apparent warning about a broken neck becomes Taiga's own threat, with a snapping demonstration before the final identification of the agent.

RM-S05A-F008.description: The classmates still want Shirou's food, but the English replaces the joke that his lunch determines cafeteria attendance with a request that he join them.
RM-S05A-F008.explanation: The classmates still want Shirou's food, but the English replaces the joke that his lunch determines cafeteria attendance with a request that he join them.
RM-S05A-F008.sourceReading: Whether Shirou brings a packed lunch substantially changes who joins the cafeteria group.

RM-TDSP-F001.description: The strange field of butter becomes a conventional field of flowers. The bath's deadly comfort remains; the specific absurd image does not.
RM-TDSP-F001.explanation: The strange field of butter becomes a conventional field of flowers. The bath's deadly comfort remains; the specific absurd image does not.
RM-TDSP-F001.sourceReading: Taiga glimpses an incongruous field of butter while the bath threatens to send her to heaven.

RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F011.description: 'Gut feeling' preserves the premonition but loses the repeated insect wording connecting it to the chirping. This finding rests on the intact quoted lines, not the damaged continuation.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F011.explanation: 'Gut feeling' preserves the premonition but loses the repeated insect wording connecting it to the chirping. This finding rests on the intact quoted lines, not the damaged continuation.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F011.sourceReading: The intact earlier anchors identify an unseasonable insect sound. 虫の報せ then links that literal insect to the idiom for a premonition.

RM-HF-D10D-F020.description: The hammer-blow shock becomes a moment of understanding. That changes Shirou's reaction, but these pages do not establish a lost joke mechanism.
RM-HF-D10D-F020.explanation: The hammer-blow shock becomes a moment of understanding. That changes Shirou's reaction, but these pages do not establish a lost joke mechanism.
RM-HF-D10D-F020.sourceReading: Rin's offer hits Shirou like a hammer blow; he then recognizes his extraordinary good fortune.

RM-R9A-F009.description: English denies benefit to others where the proverb introduces benefit returning to the giver. This belongs in a meaning or reasoning dossier rather than this dossier on jokes.
RM-R9A-F009.explanation: English denies benefit to others where the proverb introduces benefit returning to the giver. This belongs in a meaning or reasoning dossier rather than this dossier on jokes.
RM-R9A-F009.sourceReading: The proverb introduces the benefits that kindness returns to its giver, developed through the following account of circulation and replenishment.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F005.description: The household-spirit joke becomes a brownie-points joke about seeking approval. The cake association remains, but Shirou's explanation of his competence answers a different question.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F005.explanation: The household-spirit joke becomes a brownie-points joke about seeking approval. The cake association remains, but Shirou's explanation of his competence answers a different question.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F005.sourceReading: The boss asks whether the unusually helpful Shirou is a brownie, while eating a brown cake. Shirou explains his ability through experience and familiarity.

RM-HF-D10E-F005.description: Shirou's criticism of his tangled reasoning becomes a joke about protesting too much. It makes the denial sound suspicious without establishing that Rin's insinuation is true.
RM-HF-D10E-F005.explanation: Shirou's criticism of his tangled reasoning becomes a joke about protesting too much. It makes the denial sound suspicious without establishing that Rin's insinuation is true.
RM-HF-D10E-F005.sourceReading: Shirou recognizes that his explanation has lurched from instinctive choice to a claim about being Illya's guardian.

RM-HF-D10G-F018.description: Shirou asks the priest to pray for him; English has Shirou undertake the prayer himself. The wish survives, but the priest-directed banter loses its specific target.
RM-HF-D10G-F018.explanation: Shirou asks the priest to pray for him; English has Shirou undertake the prayer himself. The wish survives, but the priest-directed banter loses its specific target.
RM-HF-D10G-F018.sourceReading: Shirou asks Father Kotomine to pray that there will be no fourth occasion, combining thanks with a pointed request suited to a priest.

RM-R04F-F002.description: Saber still reads Shirou's alarm correctly, but her precise comparison of one startled syllable with two becomes a general remark about his noises.
RM-R04F-F002.explanation: Saber still reads Shirou's alarm correctly, but her precise comparison of one startled syllable with two becomes a general remark about his noises.
RM-R04F-F002.sourceReading: Saber explicitly compares a first startled sound with its doubled successor, then infers that Shirou wants to hide something.

RM-HF-D10H-F023.description: Sakura's promise to strike back at Rin with Shirou-taught cooking becomes a promise to make his favorites. Her grin and the following mock battle talk remain, but their setup is missing.
RM-HF-D10H-F023.explanation: Sakura's promise to strike back at Rin with Shirou-taught cooking becomes a promise to make his favorites. Her grin and the following mock battle talk remain, but their setup is missing.
RM-HF-D10H-F023.sourceReading: Sakura proposes playful retaliation against Rin through a breakfast made using what Shirou taught her. Her mischievous grin and their subsequent talk of striking back confirm the competitive framing.

RM-FATE-D7-ALT-CONVERSATIONS-F020.description: English keeps Shirou's teasing objection but drops his indication that he means it in a different sense. Neither version here explains that alternative concern.
RM-FATE-D7-ALT-CONVERSATIONS-F020.explanation: English keeps Shirou's teasing objection but drops his indication that he means it in a different sense. Neither version here explains that alternative concern.
RM-FATE-D7-ALT-CONVERSATIONS-F020.sourceReading: After Saber rejects the world-domination caricature, Shirou says that in a different sense Rin in particular must not receive the Grail. He does not explain that different sense.

RM-HF-D4-MIDNIGHT-F005.description: Kotomine's joke that gratitude must mean Shirou has a fever becomes a taunt about how hard thanking him is. The sarcasm remains, but its premise and medical connection change.
RM-HF-D4-MIDNIGHT-F005.explanation: Kotomine's joke that gratitude must mean Shirou has a fever becomes a taunt about how hard thanking him is. The sarcasm remains, but its premise and medical connection change.
RM-HF-D4-MIDNIGHT-F005.sourceReading: Kotomine treats Shirou's unexpected gratitude as a possible symptom of fever, then offers consultation after discussing his treatment of an injured woman.

RM-R10C-F002.description: 'Weak point' becomes 'what you find dull,' including in Saber's reply. The exchange loses the overlap between food preferences and a fighter's vulnerability.
RM-R10C-F002.explanation: 'Weak point' becomes 'what you find dull,' including in Saber's reply. The exchange loses the overlap between food preferences and a fighter's vulnerability.
RM-R10C-F002.sourceReading: Shirou moves from food preferences to wanting Saber's 'weak point.' Saber repeats that term suspiciously before he returns to practical dietary questions.

RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F014.description: Shirou jokes that moving first leaves Rin vulnerable to an opponent's late throw. English turns this into a general difficulty reacting to others, losing the game's specific trick.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F014.explanation: Shirou jokes that moving first leaves Rin vulnerable to an opponent's late throw. English turns this into a general difficulty reacting to others, losing the game's specific trick.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F014.sourceReading: Rin likes moving first; Shirou turns that preference into a rock-paper-scissors joke about being vulnerable to someone else's late throw.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F002.description: Shinji's mock praise of Shirou's spectacularly bad timing becomes surprise that an incompetent person has made it this far.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F002.explanation: Shinji's mock praise of Shirou's spectacularly bad timing becomes surprise that an incompetent person has made it this far.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F002.sourceReading: Shinji sarcastically says Shirou's extraordinarily bad timing has reached the point of being a talent.

RM-R10E-F005.description: Rin originally points out that Shirou's defense itself proves how blunt he is. English makes her say the remark was predictable, changing the punchline.
RM-R10E-F005.explanation: Rin originally points out that Shirou's defense itself proves how blunt he is. English makes her say the remark was predictable, changing the punchline.
RM-R10E-F005.sourceReading: Shirou's claim that he copied Rin's indirectness itself bluntly criticizes her. Rin points to that very response as evidence of his directness.

RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F017.description: “Tohsaka say” needs a verb correction. The passage still conveys Rin's displeasure at Shirou's growing closeness with Saber.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F017.explanation: “Tohsaka say” needs a verb correction. The passage still conveys Rin's displeasure at Shirou's growing closeness with Saber.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F017.sourceReading: Shirou notices that Rin speaks with the same displeasure she displayed at dinner.

RM-P3-001.description: “Shoddy work” makes Rin criticize poor workmanship after she has dismissed skill level as irrelevant. The Japanese instead condemns the thing planted in her territory as vile.
RM-P3-001.explanation: “Shoddy work” makes Rin criticize poor workmanship after she has dismissed skill level as irrelevant. The Japanese instead condemns the thing planted in her territory as vile.
RM-P3-001.sourceReading: Rin dismisses the maker's skill level as irrelevant and condemns the vile thing installed in her territory.

RM-S09G-F007.description: Rin originally uses Shirou's assurance that the treatment is not his concern to press him onward. “You don't want the procedure? Well, too bad” makes her dismiss an objection instead.
RM-S09G-F007.explanation: Rin originally uses Shirou's assurance that the treatment is not his concern to press him onward. “You don't want the procedure? Well, too bad” makes her dismiss an objection instead.
RM-S09G-F007.sourceReading: Rin checks that the rough treatment itself is not his objection, echoing his explicit statement two pages earlier, and tells him to submit to it.

RM-S0305-F009.description: The Japanese describes Rin's present manner as harsh and standoffish. The English assigns those qualities to her school persona, reversing the contrast Shirou notices.
RM-S0305-F009.explanation: The Japanese describes Rin's present manner as harsh and standoffish. The English assigns those qualities to her school persona, reversing the contrast Shirou notices.
RM-S0305-F009.sourceReading: The Rin standing before Shirou is harsh and standoffish, strikingly different from the Rin he sees at school. He nevertheless recognizes the kindness behind her help.

RM-HF-D10C-F005.description: Rin still ends the deadlock first, but break the ice omits her release of her fighting stance. Both versions keep Shirou lowering his wooden sword after her request.
RM-HF-D10C-F005.explanation: Rin still ends the deadlock first, but break the ice omits her release of her fighting stance. Both versions keep Shirou lowering his wooden sword after her request.
RM-HF-D10C-F005.sourceReading: Rin asks Shirou to lower the sword and is the first to release her stance; he then lowers his wooden sword. The omitted detail is her physical de-escalation, not all of her initiative.

RM-R14O-F008.description: “At an advantage” reverses Rin's position. The Japanese places her under pressure alongside Shirou, with the added burden of understanding how badly she is outmatched.
RM-R14O-F008.explanation: “At an advantage” reverses Rin's position. The Japanese places her under pressure alongside Shirou, with the added burden of understanding how badly she is outmatched.
RM-R14O-F008.sourceReading: Rin is at a disadvantage too; understanding the disparity in strength makes her burden greater than Shirou's.

RM-S0512A-F006.description: The Japanese explicitly gives Rin a smile before she turns triumphantly toward Shirou. The English describes the diners' happy faces instead; the claim that her attention is exclusively on Sakura is less certain.
RM-S0512A-F006.explanation: The Japanese explicitly gives Rin a smile before she turns triumphantly toward Shirou. The English describes the diners' happy faces instead; the claim that her attention is exclusively on Sakura is less certain.
RM-S0512A-F006.sourceReading: Rin watches with a smile after Sakura's delighted response, then turns triumphantly toward Shirou. The demonstrative can also encompass the meal's favorable reception.

RM-P2-008.description: The English replaces Rin's account of leading a follower around with visits to useful minor landmarks. It loses her deliberate handling of the follower, without establishing whether she evades or identifies anyone.
RM-P2-008.explanation: The English replaces Rin's account of leading a follower around with visits to useful minor landmarks. It loses her deliberate handling of the follower, without establishing whether she evades or identifies anyone.
RM-P2-008.sourceReading: Rin visits the main places and thoroughly leads the person following her around before dinner and the final stop. Archer's preceding reference to small fry following her supports an outside pursuer.

RM-R7D-008.description: “Find out a deep part of her” is awkward phrasing for coming to understand her more deeply. The surrounding passage preserves Shirou's recognition of her kindness.
RM-R7D-008.explanation: “Find out a deep part of her” is awkward phrasing for coming to understand her more deeply. The surrounding passage preserves Shirou's recognition of her kindness.
RM-R7D-008.sourceReading: Shirou feels he glimpsed a deeper side of Rin through her distress at the collapsed students.

RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F013.description: The English preserves Rin standing there but drops her blank, distracted manner. The passage does not establish why she is in that state.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F013.explanation: The English preserves Rin standing there but drops her blank, distracted manner. The passage does not establish why she is in that state.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F013.sourceReading: Shirou turns back toward Rin, who is still standing blankly or absentmindedly, before greeting her and following Issei.

RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F013.description: The English keeps Shirou's teasing objection but drops his explicit “in a different sense” qualification and softens its insistence. The Japanese does not explain what that different concern is.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F013.explanation: The English keeps Shirou's teasing objection but drops his explicit “in a different sense” qualification and softens its insistence. The Japanese does not explain what that different concern is.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F013.sourceReading: Shirou jokingly singles Rin out as someone who must not receive the Grail, in a different sense from the world-domination concern Saber has answered.

RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F004.description: “Anyway” removes Shirou's reservation about Rin's teaching aptitude. Her enthusiasm consequently reads more like evidence that she will be a good teacher.
RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F004.explanation: “Anyway” removes Shirou's reservation about Rin's teaching aptitude. Her enthusiasm consequently reads more like evidence that she will be a good teacher.
RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F004.sourceReading: Shirou notices Rin's enthusiasm for teaching, contrasts her with Saber, then explicitly sets aside whether Rin is suited to the job.

RM-HF-D10E-F001.description: Shirou still protests Rin's silence, but the English drops his reminder that she asked for his answer in the first place.
RM-HF-D10E-F001.explanation: Shirou still protests Rin's silence, but the English drops his reminder that she asked for his answer in the first place.
RM-HF-D10E-F001.sourceReading: Shirou complains that Rin has prompted his response and then fallen silent when he gives it.

RM-R04D-F009.description: Shirou's surprise at Rin's efficiency becomes surprise at her kindness. His more specific surprise that she owns ladylike clothes also becomes a broader judgment about her mature taste.
RM-R04D-F009.explanation: Shirou's surprise at Rin's efficiency becomes surprise at her kindness. His more specific surprise that she owns ladylike clothes also becomes a broader judgment about her mature taste.
RM-R04D-F009.sourceReading: Shirou is surprised by Rin's efficient arrangements—or, more precisely, that these ladylike clothes belong to her.

RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F005.description: Ayako's complaint about Shirou being excessively dutiful becomes a complaint about excessive honesty. Sakura's preceding description of him as a stickler still preserves some of the original point.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F005.explanation: Ayako's complaint about Shirou being excessively dutiful becomes a complaint about excessive honesty. Sakura's preceding description of him as a stickler still preserves some of the original point.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F005.sourceReading: Ayako's reported complaint concerns excessive conscientiousness despite Shirou's rough manners. His insistence on being awake before Sakura arrives supplies the immediate example.

RM-P1-019.description: A description of when Ayako's masculine manner emerges becomes Rin announcing her own candor. The link between Ayako's feelings and her changing voice disappears.
RM-P1-019.explanation: A description of when Ayako's masculine manner emerges becomes Rin announcing her own candor. The link between Ayako's feelings and her changing voice disappears.
RM-P1-019.sourceReading: Rin describes Ayako's speech becoming masculine when her genuine feelings come through, immediately after Ayako enthusiastically pulls her toward tea.

RM-R04E-F006.description: The reflexive should agree with 'those.' This is a sentence-level grammar issue, without a demonstrated change to Ayako's characterization.
RM-R04E-F006.explanation: The reflexive should agree with 'those.' This is a sentence-level grammar issue, without a demonstrated change to Ayako's characterization.
RM-R04E-F006.sourceReading: Ayako says that someone unable to face and pierce their own self cannot understand the discipline's spirit.

RM-P1-024.description: Rin's tentative thought that Ayako has lacked interest becomes a firmer explanation that she has not found the right person. The preceding conversation supports that possibility without establishing it.
RM-P1-024.explanation: Rin's tentative thought that Ayako has lacked interest becomes a firmer explanation that she has not found the right person. The preceding conversation supports that possibility without establishing it.
RM-P1-024.sourceReading: Rin considers whether Ayako has simply lacked interest until now, rather than disliking men.

RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F007.description: Ayako's presumed higher formal rank becomes presumed superior ability. Both versions remain inferential, so the change concerns what is compared rather than a conversion to certainty.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F007.explanation: Ayako's presumed higher formal rank becomes presumed superior ability. Both versions remain inferential, so the change concerns what is compared rather than a conversion to certainty.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F007.sourceReading: Shirou supposes that Ayako's formal rank is now higher, despite her continuing determination to impress him.

RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-F012.description: Ten tiles become ten stacks of tiles, enlarging Rin's comic threat. The sarcastic delight and playful pressure on Shirou remain.
RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-F012.explanation: Ten tiles become ten stacks of tiles, enlarging Rin's comic threat. The sarcastic delight and playful pressure on Shirou remain.
RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-F012.sourceReading: Rin sarcastically imagines Ayako being delighted enough to smash through ten tiles.

RM-S0207-F002.description: A first-year class connection becomes a relationship continuing 'since' first year. The Japanese sentence establishes their past familiarity without making that continuing claim.
RM-S0207-F002.explanation: A first-year class connection becomes a relationship continuing 'since' first year. The Japanese sentence establishes their past familiarity without making that continuing claim.
RM-S0207-F002.sourceReading: Shirou identifies Ayako as someone who was his classmate in their first year.

RM-S0207-F012.description: The English redirects Ayako's barbed remark from Rin to Shinji. Shirou's following suspicion that Ayako may be Rin's enemy consequently loses its immediate basis.
RM-S0207-F012.explanation: The English redirects Ayako's barbed remark from Rin to Shinji. Shirou's following suspicion that Ayako may be Rin's enemy consequently loses its immediate basis.
RM-S0207-F012.sourceReading: Ayako suggests that the aloof Rin might benefit from an unpleasant experience. Shirou immediately wonders whether Ayako is one of Rin's enemies.

RM-R04I-F001.description: The explicit difficulty of sustained practice becomes a measure of duration. This passage concerns Shirou's training and does not support the proposed Ayako dossier.
RM-R04I-F001.explanation: The explicit difficulty of sustained practice becomes a measure of duration. This passage concerns Shirou's training and does not support the proposed Ayako dossier.
RM-R04I-F001.sourceReading: Shirou describes the demanding task of sustaining accuracy and penetration over time.

RM-R6B-F001.description: The English removes the timing and restricted source of the gossip, adds deliberate secrecy, and makes hurting Ayako the stated purpose. These changes belong in a discussion of Shinji and Shirou's interpretation of him.
RM-R6B-F001.explanation: The English removes the timing and restricted source of the gossip, adds deliberate secrecy, and makes hurting Ayako the stated purpose. These changes belong in a discussion of Shinji and Shirou's interpretation of him.
RM-R6B-F001.sourceReading: Shirou objects to entertaining gossip already circulating yesterday about information supposedly restricted to Ayako's rescuers. He suspects Shinji spread it knowing its harmful effects.

RM-P1-023.description: Ayako's assurance that they will accept defeat becomes a claim that both are sore losers. Their promise to honor the wager survives, but the stated basis of that promise is reversed.
RM-P1-023.explanation: Ayako's assurance that they will accept defeat becomes a claim that both are sore losers. Their promise to honor the wager survives, but the stated basis of that promise is reversed.
RM-P1-023.sourceReading: Ayako says that neither of them will refuse to accept defeat, then confidently anticipates the loser's compliance.

RM-P1-031.description: Ayako's role in keeping unruly members in line becomes assigning them grunt work. This introduces a method and changes how she describes her remaining value as captain.
RM-P1-031.explanation: Ayako's role in keeping unruly members in line becomes assigning them grunt work. This introduces a method and changes how she describes her remaining value as captain.
RM-P1-031.sourceReading: Ayako self-deprecatingly says that keeping troublesome members under control is the only useful thing she can do as captain.

RM-P1-032.description: Ayako's decision to stop dwelling on the former member becomes an explanation that discounts Fujimura's praise. Her eventual resolve remains, but the step leading to it changes.
RM-P1-032.explanation: Ayako's decision to stop dwelling on the former member becomes an explanation that discounts Fujimura's praise. Her eventual resolve remains, but the step leading to it changes.
RM-P1-032.sourceReading: Ayako decides there is no use dwelling on the departed member and responds to Fujimura's praise by resolving to take her captaincy seriously.

RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-C011.description: Rin adapts the treatment and explicitly offers to stop if Shirou refuses.
RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-C011.explanation: Rin adapts the treatment and explicitly offers to stop if Shirou refuses.

RM-R04A-C006.description: Rin’s severe instruction to treat even family as enemy Masters remains explicit.
RM-R04A-C006.explanation: Rin’s severe instruction to treat even family as enemy Masters remains explicit.

RM-P1-C013.description: Rin’s aversion to eliminating witnesses remains the stated reason for keeping social ties superficial.
RM-P1-C013.explanation: Rin’s aversion to eliminating witnesses remains the stated reason for keeping social ties superficial.

RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-C007.description: Rin makes the arrangement; Shirou recognizes that she did something he should have done, and her guarded explanation follows.
RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-C007.explanation: Rin makes the arrangement; Shirou recognizes that she did something he should have done, and her guarded explanation follows.

RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-C009.description: Sakura explicitly reports Ayako’s complaint, and Shirou recognizes who has been criticizing him.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-C009.explanation: Sakura explicitly reports Ayako’s complaint, and Shirou recognizes who has been criticizing him.

RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-C022.description: Shirou credits Ayako’s work while Shinji claims the credit for himself; the boast remains speaker-bound.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-C022.explanation: Shirou credits Ayako’s work while Shinji claims the credit for himself; the boast remains speaker-bound.

RM-R04E-C003.description: Ayako’s belief that Shirou lost interest remains her stated interpretation, not an established account of his motive.
RM-R04E-C003.explanation: Ayako’s belief that Shirou lost interest remains her stated interpretation, not an established account of his motive.

RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-C011.description: The report of Ayako’s injury remains distinct from the others’ expectation that she would fight back.
RM-FATE-D7-MORNING-C011.explanation: The report of Ayako’s injury remains distinct from the others’ expectation that she would fight back.

RM-R7E-012.description: Rin's final dismissal changes “harmless” to “not even an annoyance.” Her earlier explanation still preserves his inability to hurt anyone, so this is a local change in the insult.
RM-R7E-012.explanation: Rin's final dismissal changes “harmless” to “not even an annoyance.” Her earlier explanation still preserves his inability to hurt anyone, so this is a local change in the insult.
RM-R7E-012.sourceReading: Rin mockingly calls Shinji harmless because he is neither a mage nor fit to be a Master. She presents not calling him a harmful pest as a concession.

RM-P1-034.description: Rin's claim that she never noticed Shinji at the range becomes a claim that she did not know he belonged to the club, although she has already corrected his club title.
RM-P1-034.explanation: Rin's claim that she never noticed Shinji at the range becomes a claim that she did not know he belonged to the club, although she has already corrected his club title.
RM-P1-034.sourceReading: Rin says she only now learned that Shinji had been at the shooting area, using her failure to notice him to underline her disinterest.

RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F015.description: Shinji's insult changes Shirou from Issei's toady into his victim or scapegoat. This alters the sneer, not the established facts of their friendship.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F015.explanation: Shinji's insult changes Shirou from Issei's toady into his victim or scapegoat. This alters the sneer, not the established facts of their friendship.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F015.sourceReading: Shinji derides Shirou as Ryudou's flatterer or toady after leaving the club.

RM-S08C-F016.description: Rin's explanation loses the excessive self-love that she says produces Shinji's contempt. The contrast with her preceding description of self-hatred is consequently less explicit.
RM-S08C-F016.explanation: Rin's explanation loses the excessive self-love that she says produces Shinji's contempt. The contrast with her preceding description of self-hatred is consequently less explicit.
RM-S08C-F016.sourceReading: Rin says excessive love of himself led Shinji to look down on others, whose superiority then trapped him in inferiority. This follows her description of a disposition involving self-hatred.

RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F009.description: Shinji's explicit claim to equal Rin becomes general boasting about being a Master. This weakens the direct link between his claim and Rin's reply that Shirou qualifies too.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F009.explanation: Shinji's explicit claim to equal Rin becomes general boasting about being a Master. This weakens the direct link between his claim and Rin's reply that Shirou qualifies too.
RM-FATE-D7-BATH-RIN-SHINJI-F009.sourceReading: Rin reports Shinji boasting that becoming a Master makes him equal to her; she answers that Shirou is therefore equal too.

RM-R14U-F013.description: The English replaces Shinji's unsteady steps with eagerness. His excitement fits the scene, but the bodily instability accompanying his loss of restraint disappears.
RM-R14U-F013.explanation: The English replaces Shinji's unsteady steps with eagerness. His excitement fits the scene, but the bodily instability accompanying his loss of restraint disappears.
RM-R14U-F013.sourceReading: Shinji approaches Rin with unsteady steps as his rational restraint is coming undone.

RM-S09A-F010.description: Shinji's boast about winning now without Saber becomes another excuse for his earlier defeat. This also weakens the stated basis for Shirou's next inference about what Shinji knows.
RM-S09A-F010.explanation: Shinji's boast about winning now without Saber becomes another excuse for his earlier defeat. This also weakens the stated basis for Shirou's next inference about what Shinji knows.
RM-S09A-F010.sourceReading: After excusing his earlier retreat, Shinji claims that even now he cannot lose provided Saber does not appear.

RM-S09D-F002.description: Shinji's dismissal of the danger to Rider becomes an assertion that Servants die easily. The English reverses his stated answer to Shirou's warning.
RM-S09D-F002.explanation: Shinji's dismissal of the danger to Rider becomes an assertion that Servants die easily. The English reverses his stated answer to Shirou's warning.
RM-S09D-F002.sourceReading: Shinji rhetorically denies that Servants are the sort to die easily, rejecting Shirou's warning that Rider cannot endure more.

RM-R14X-F004.description: Shinji's complaint that Lancer took Rin from him becomes a complaint that Lancer “got” him. This obscures the possessive grievance, although it need not refer only to his injury.
RM-R14X-F004.explanation: Shinji's complaint that Lancer took Rin from him becomes a complaint that Lancer “got” him. This obscures the possessive grievance, although it need not refer only to his injury.
RM-R14X-F004.sourceReading: Following the statement that Rin escaped, Shinji complains about having her taken from him by someone who was nearly dead.

RM-S09G-F016.description: Shinji's boast that he would win becomes an admission that Shirou would win. This changes the self-serving argument with which he sends Rider against Shirou.
RM-S09G-F016.explanation: Shinji's boast that he would win becomes an admission that Shirou would win. This changes the self-serving argument with which he sends Rider against Shirou.
RM-S09G-F016.sourceReading: Shinji claims that he himself would certainly win an ordinary fight, before presenting combat against Rider as fair.

RM-R5D-F004.description: Failure to reach Shinji becomes a claim that he has not been home. The passage supports a local change in reported knowledge, but not the proposed character dossier.
RM-R5D-F004.explanation: Failure to reach Shinji becomes a claim that he has not been home. The passage supports a local change in reported knowledge, but not the proposed character dossier.
RM-R5D-F004.sourceReading: Shirou says he understands that Shinji cannot be reached or found, while asking who has failed to return home.

RM-S0215-F006.description: The English specifies an action by Sakura as the cause of Shinji's displeasure. The Japanese leaves that cause unstated; neither wording makes his violence justified.
RM-S0215-F006.explanation: The English specifies an action by Sakura as the cause of Shinji's displeasure. The Japanese leaves that cause unstated; neither wording makes his violence justified.
RM-S0215-F006.sourceReading: Shinji says he hit Sakura simply because he was displeased. The object or cause of that displeasure is unstated.

RM-S11E-F013.description: What shaped Shinji becomes something he constructed in his head. The family revelation still overturns his self-image, but the sentence shifts emphasis toward his own mental construction.
RM-S11E-F013.explanation: What shaped Shinji becomes something he constructed in his head. The family revelation still overturns his self-image, but the sentence shifts emphasis toward his own mental construction.
RM-S11E-F013.sourceReading: The revelation overturns both what Shinji believed and what had shaped him.

RM-R7D7-002.description: Shirou's advice loses its condition that Shinji is not going to fight. Staying home becomes general advice for self-protection.
RM-R7D7-002.explanation: Shirou's advice loses its condition that Shinji is not going to fight. Staying home becomes general advice for self-protection.
RM-R7D7-002.sourceReading: Shirou recalls advising Shinji to stay home and protect himself if he is not going to fight.

RM-S0505-F003.description: Shinji's sneer at Sakura's unsophisticated earnestness becomes a dismissal of her explanation as bullshit. His demand that she obey him remains.
RM-S0505-F003.explanation: Shinji's sneer at Sakura's unsophisticated earnestness becomes a dismissal of her explanation as bullshit. His demand that she obey him remains.
RM-S0505-F003.sourceReading: Shinji disparages Sakura as unsophisticated or gracelessly earnest for invoking her duty as a junior.

RM-R9C-F005.description: “Placenta” becomes “organism.” The English retains Shinji's disgust but removes the specific image reducing his mother to a reproductive organ.
RM-R9C-F005.explanation: “Placenta” becomes “organism.” The English retains Shinji's disgust but removes the specific image reducing his mother to a reproductive organ.
RM-R9C-F005.sourceReading: The narration, presenting Shinji's contempt, reduces his mother to a placenta that produced his inferior self.

RM-HF-D10B-F003.description: The English changes a warning that silence could cause irreparable harm into an expectation that speaking will change things. This belongs in a review of Shirou's decision to warn Illya.
RM-HF-D10B-F003.explanation: The English changes a warning that silence could cause irreparable harm into an expectation that speaking will change things. This belongs in a review of Shirou's decision to warn Illya.
RM-HF-D10B-F003.sourceReading: Shirou expects irreparable consequences unless he tells Illya about both dangers.

RM-HF-D10C-F026.description: Zouken's claim that shared order no longer holds becomes a claim that he follows a universal law. This changes the reasoning by which he excuses sacrificing others for survival.
RM-HF-D10C-F026.explanation: Zouken's claim that shared order no longer holds becomes a claim that he follows a universal law. This changes the reasoning by which he excuses sacrificing others for survival.
RM-HF-D10C-F026.sourceReading: Zouken says that no sustaining order of interconnection can hold under humanity's destructive greed, then uses inevitable collapse to excuse breaking step himself.

RM-HF-D10D-F019.description: The shared objective survives, but the English leaves out Rin's explicit limit: cooperating until Zouken is defeated.
RM-HF-D10D-F019.explanation: The shared objective survives, but the English leaves out Rin's explicit limit: cooperating until Zouken is defeated.
RM-HF-D10D-F019.sourceReading: Rin offers cooperation until their shared objective of defeating Zouken is achieved.

RM-HF-D10F-F008.description: The English treats Saber becoming Zouken's Servant as established and leaves only the mechanism unknown. The Japanese leaves the relationship itself uncertain.
RM-HF-D10F-F008.explanation: The English treats Saber becoming Zouken's Servant as established and leaves only the mechanism unknown. The Japanese leaves the relationship itself uncertain.
RM-HF-D10F-F008.sourceReading: Shirou does not know whether Saber has become Zouken's Servant; only her hostility is established.

RM-HF-D14B-F039.description: The English increases the distance between the two men's objectives from somewhat better to a lot better. Shirou still rejects Kotomine's objective in the next line.
RM-HF-D14B-F039.explanation: The English increases the distance between the two men's objectives from somewhat better to a lot better. Shirou still rejects Kotomine's objective in the next line.
RM-HF-D14B-F039.sourceReading: Shirou regards Kotomine's objective as somewhat preferable to Zouken's, while still rejecting it.

RM-S07G-F003.description: Shirou's prediction that Zouken will intervene becomes a declaration that Shirou himself cannot stand aside. Zouken's anticipated initiative disappears from this sentence.
RM-S07G-F003.explanation: Shirou's prediction that Zouken will intervene becomes a declaration that Shirou himself cannot stand aside. Zouken's anticipated initiative disappears from this sentence.
RM-S07G-F003.sourceReading: The blood-feeding monster who sought the Grail through Shinji cannot be expected to remain a passive spectator.

RM-S07J-F007.description: The English replaces a judgment about Zouken's departure from ordinary human bounds with a specific claim that he has lost sight of his goal. The passage instead links his altered mentality to prolonged decay.
RM-S07J-F007.explanation: The English replaces a judgment about Zouken's departure from ordinary human bounds with a specific claim that he has lost sight of his goal. The passage instead links his altered mentality to prolonged decay.
RM-S07J-F007.sourceReading: The narration speculates that Zouken has long departed from ordinary human bounds, then explains the incomprehensible mental effects of centuries of bodily decay.

RM-S08A-F013.description: Zouken's almost visible killing intent becomes hostility in the surrounding insects. His chuckle remains, but the direct description of his murderous intent is lost.
RM-S08A-F013.explanation: Zouken's almost visible killing intent becomes hostility in the surrounding insects. His chuckle remains, but the direct description of his murderous intent is lost.
RM-S08A-F013.sourceReading: The old insect-user laughs with killing intent so palpable that it seems visible.

RM-S11C-F010.description: Rin's observation that the scene has not been cleaned becomes a claim that Zouken cannot clean it. Her conclusion that he was absent survives, but its stated evidential basis changes.
RM-S11C-F010.explanation: Rin's observation that the scene has not been cleaned becomes a claim that Zouken cannot clean it. Her conclusion that he was absent survives, but its stated evidential basis changes.
RM-S11C-F010.sourceReading: Rin points to the unfinished cleanup as evidence that Zouken was absent: he would not have left body parts behind.

RM-S13A-F005.description: Zouken's wretched continued life remains, but his claim to be the only collaborator still living is omitted. This weakens the contrast between the original shared undertaking and his solitary persistence.
RM-S13A-F005.explanation: Zouken's wretched continued life remains, but his claim to be the only collaborator still living is omitted. This weakens the contrast between the original shared undertaking and his solitary persistence.
RM-S13A-F005.sourceReading: Zouken says that he alone among those who joined hands still continues his wretched existence.

RM-S0214-F003.description: Zouken claims to intervene at his grandchild's request. The English instead has him threaten Shirou despite what his granddaughter might want, reversing the family justification he offers.
RM-S0214-F003.explanation: Zouken claims to intervene at his grandchild's request. The English instead has him threaten Shirou despite what his granddaughter might want, reversing the family justification he offers.
RM-S0214-F003.sourceReading: Zouken invokes his grandchild's request as his reason for not overlooking the supposed suspicious outsider.

RM-S15A-F013.description: Shirou's expectation that all the pieces will be at his destination becomes a statement that Zouken has his pawns in hand. This shifts the tactical emphasis from gathering to possession without proving total control over anyone.
RM-S15A-F013.explanation: Shirou's expectation that all the pieces will be at his destination becomes a statement that Zouken has his pawns in hand. This shifts the tactical emphasis from gathering to possession without proving total control over anyone.
RM-S15A-F013.sourceReading: Given Zouken's presumed interest in Illya, Shirou should expect all the pieces to be assembled at his destination.

RM-S15I-F007.description: The accusation against Kotomine changes from exploiting Sakura to deceiving her, and the thing's unknown nature becomes Sakura's ignorance. This belongs with Kotomine and Sakura rather than serving as proof of Zouken's methods.
RM-S15I-F007.explanation: The accusation against Kotomine changes from exploiting Sakura to deceiving her, and the thing's unknown nature becomes Sakura's ignorance. This belongs with Kotomine and Sakura rather than serving as proof of Zouken's methods.
RM-S15I-F007.sourceReading: Shirou accuses Kotomine of using Sakura to create something uncanny or unidentified and then appropriating it.

RM-S15I-F021.description: Illya's inability to escape her inherited purpose becomes Zouken's refusal to let her escape. The later cooperation lines partly preserve his reasoning, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of it.
RM-S15I-F021.explanation: Illya's inability to escape her inherited purpose becomes Zouken's refusal to let her escape. The later cooperation lines partly preserve his reasoning, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of it.
RM-S15I-F021.sourceReading: The narration presents Zouken's confidence that Illya cannot escape her inherited purpose: even if released, she will cooperate and come to the Grail's heart herself.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F014.description: Zouken's theatrical claim that he must die for Shinji becomes a promise to risk himself. The family obligation remains, but the announced sacrifice is less absolute.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F014.explanation: Zouken's theatrical claim that he must die for Shinji becomes a promise to risk himself. The family obligation remains, but the announced sacrifice is less absolute.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F014.sourceReading: Zouken theatrically announces that he must die, then says he must save his blood relative even at the cost of his own body.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F016.description: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F016.explanation: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F016.sourceReading: Zouken says he learned the Grail would appear and had his grandson contract in his place. He then addresses Shirou as someone belonging to a magical lineage.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F018.description: Zouken's claim that he has been away for roughly ten years disappears. The same interval instead describes the apprentice's growth, changing his explanation for his limited knowledge.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F018.explanation: Zouken's claim that he has been away for roughly ten years disappears. The same interval instead describes the apprentice's growth, changing his explanation for his limited knowledge.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F018.sourceReading: Zouken attributes his unfamiliarity with the previous head's apprentice to having been away for about ten years.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F019.description: Uncertainty about Zouken's feelings toward the Tohsakas becomes amusement at their presumed feelings. This supplies a target for his laughter that the Japanese leaves open.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F019.explanation: Uncertainty about Zouken's feelings toward the Tohsakas becomes amusement at their presumed feelings. This supplies a target for his laughter that the Japanese leaves open.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F019.sourceReading: Shirou cannot tell what feelings Zouken holds toward the Tohsaka family as Zouken laughs with apparent pleasure.

RM-S0316-F010.description: The English preserves Shirou's fear of an immediate attack but drops the jubilation he imagines in his pursuer. This changes Shirou's perception of Lancer, without proving Lancer actually feels that delight.
RM-S0316-F010.explanation: The English preserves Shirou's fear of an immediate attack but drops the jubilation he imagines in his pursuer. This changes Shirou's perception of Lancer, without proving Lancer actually feels that delight.
RM-S0316-F010.sourceReading: Shirou imagines his pursuer rushing in with apparent jubilation if he screams.

RM-R14L-F007.description: Lancer's admission that Rin's gratitude dazzles him becomes praise of her as a Master. His loyalty constraint remains, but the personal effect of her thanks is less specific.
RM-R14L-F007.explanation: Lancer's admission that Rin's gratitude dazzles him becomes praise of her as a Master. His loyalty constraint remains, but the personal effect of her thanks is less specific.
RM-R14L-F007.sourceReading: Speaking as someone who cannot readily betray his own master, Lancer finds the gratitude just described a little dazzling.

RM-S1517B-F016.description: The English adds a physical advance into Saber's reach where the Japanese describes his killing intent reaching her. This belongs with combat staging rather than a claim about his motives.
RM-S1517B-F016.explanation: The English adds a physical advance into Saber's reach where the Japanese describes his killing intent reaching her. This belongs with combat staging rather than a claim about his motives.
RM-S1517B-F016.sourceReading: Lancer's bestial killing intent penetrates Saber's sphere; the sentence makes the intent, rather than his body, the advancing entity.

RM-S0316-F029.description: The English replaces Lancer's stagger with a foot stomp. Blocking the attack is a defensible reading, but the involuntary loss of balance is lost.
RM-S0316-F029.explanation: The English replaces Lancer's stagger with a foot stomp. Blocking the attack is a defensible reading, but the involuntary loss of balance is lost.
RM-S0316-F029.sourceReading: Lancer receives Saber's blow and staggers or takes involuntary recovery steps.

RM-R14N-F005.description: Lancer's sense that something does not add up becomes Archer's disgruntlement. This removes the thought that leads into Lancer questioning his own performance.
RM-R14N-F005.explanation: Lancer's sense that something does not add up becomes Archer's disgruntlement. This removes the thought that leads into Lancer questioning his own performance.
RM-R14N-F005.sourceReading: Lancer pauses to inspect Archer because something does not add up to him, leading into his questioning of Archer's strength and his own restraint.

RM-S0508X-F016.description: Saber's description of Lancer as inconsistent becomes a general remark that he is peculiar. The link between his temperament and his inefficient toying is weakened.
RM-S0508X-F016.explanation: Saber's description of Lancer as inconsistent becomes a general remark that he is peculiar. The link between his temperament and his inefficient toying is weakened.
RM-S0508X-F016.sourceReading: Saber tentatively describes Lancer as inconsistent or subject to moods, responding to Shirou's contrast between his efficient weapon and wasteful toying.

RM-S0508X-F018.description: The English generalizes the heart wound to a chest wound while preserving Lancer's chilling casualness. The anatomical difference belongs in a wound-focused dossier.
RM-S0508X-F018.explanation: The English generalizes the heart wound to a chest wound while preserving Lancer's chilling casualness. The anatomical difference belongs in a wound-focused dossier.
RM-S0508X-F018.sourceReading: Shirou recalls Lancer piercing his heart with the casualness of cutting grass.

RM-R14U-F012.description: The English turns an admiringly abrasive description of clinging to life into straightforward praise of legendary endurance. His persistence remains, but its rough verbal edge disappears.
RM-R14U-F012.explanation: The English turns an admiringly abrasive description of clinging to life into straightforward praise of legendary endurance. His persistence remains, but its rough verbal edge disappears.
RM-R14U-F012.sourceReading: The narration attributes Lancer's continued bodily existence to his tenacious clinging to life, using a deliberately unflattering term in quotation marks.

RM-S1517B-F017.description: The spear's flashing movement becomes a description of its light. This is an action-image change, without evidence here of a changed desire for battle.
RM-S1517B-F017.explanation: The spear's flashing movement becomes a description of its light. This is an action-image change, without evidence here of a changed desire for battle.
RM-S1517B-F017.sourceReading: Lancer's spear bursts forth as a flash, beginning the attack that Saber meets.

RM-R14U-F016.description: Lancer aiming his spear between Shinji's eyes becomes bringing his face close to Shinji's. The next page restores the spear threat, but this moment loses its precise, controlled intimidation.
RM-R14U-F016.explanation: Lancer aiming his spear between Shinji's eyes becomes bringing his face close to Shinji's. The next page restores the spear threat, but this moment loses its precise, controlled intimidation.
RM-R14U-F016.sourceReading: The object carried forward from withdrawing the spear is the spear itself: Lancer precisely aims it between Shinji's eyebrows.

RM-R14U-F017.description: Lancer still brushes off Rin's thanks, but he now attributes the rescue to personal inclination instead of how events unfolded. This changes his stated explanation, without settling his underlying motives.
RM-R14U-F017.explanation: Lancer still brushes off Rin's thanks, but he now attributes the rescue to personal inclination instead of how events unfolded. This changes his stated explanation, without settling his underlying motives.

RM-R14U-F020.description: Lancer's deeply amused murmur becomes a hearty laugh. The pleasure survives, but the farewell changes from quiet teasing to an overt burst of laughter.
RM-R14U-F020.explanation: Lancer's deeply amused murmur becomes a hearty laugh. The pleasure survives, but the farewell changes from quiet teasing to an overt burst of laughter.
RM-R14U-F020.sourceReading: Lancer's muttered reply to Rin sounds deeply amused or delighted.

RM-HF-D14C-F012.description: The English reverses who takes whom away. Illya presents herself as taking responsibility for Sakura's departure; the English makes Sakura lead Illya away.
RM-HF-D14C-F012.explanation: The English reverses who takes whom away. Illya presents herself as taking responsibility for Sakura's departure; the English makes Sakura lead Illya away.
