RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F002.description: “Hell-bent” makes Sakura's hesitation sound like stubborn determination. Shirou already presses his offer in Japanese, but the question itself asks about her preference.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F002.explanation: “Hell-bent” makes Sakura's hesitation sound like stubborn determination. Shirou already presses his offer in Japanese, but the question itself asks about her preference.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F002.sourceReading: Shirou asks whether Sakura wants to go home alone while pressing her to accept his escort.

RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F012.description: Sakura's agreement remains clear. The missing quotation marks do not demonstrate a change to her agency or relationship with Taiga.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F012.explanation: Sakura's agreement remains clear. The missing quotation marks do not demonstrate a change to her agency or relationship with Taiga.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F012.sourceReading: Sakura politely agrees provided Taiga is willing.

RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F008.description: The English substitutes delicacy for the fingers' pale color. This changes the image without establishing a change to Sakura's selfhood or agency.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F008.explanation: The English substitutes delicacy for the fingers' pale color. This changes the image without establishing a change to Sakura's selfhood or agency.
RM-FATE-D1-HOUSEHOLD-F008.sourceReading: The whiteness or paleness of Sakura's fingers catches Shirou's eye.

RM-HF-D10A-F018.description: Sakura's surprise at Rider's unsolicited concern becomes surprise that Rider has offered any suggestion. This weakens the explicit recognition of care between them.
RM-HF-D10A-F018.explanation: Sakura's surprise at Rider's unsolicited concern becomes surprise that Rider has offered any suggestion. This weakens the explicit recognition of care between them.
RM-HF-D10A-F018.sourceReading: What surprises Sakura is Rider taking the initiative to express concern for her in this way.

RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F016.description: The English supplies a specific promise about where Shirou sleeps and changes his muddled resolve into having learned a lesson. Sakura's enjoyment of waking him is still present.
RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F016.explanation: The English supplies a specific promise about where Shirou sleeps and changes his muddled resolve into having learned a lesson. Sakura's enjoyment of waking him is still present.
RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F016.sourceReading: Shirou sleepily says he will try harder next time without being discouraged by this, leaving the effort unspecified.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F014.description: The English attaches Sakura's pride to her preceding statement and omits her chest-puffing pose. It preserves her confidence but loses the physical comedy.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F014.explanation: The English attaches Sakura's pride to her preceding statement and omits her chest-puffing pose. It preserves her confidence but loses the physical comedy.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F014.sourceReading: Sakura puffs out her chest with pride after describing her gas-valve checks.

RM-HF-D10D-F017.description: Kirei questions whether Sakura is worth Shirou's life. The English instead questions whether sacrifice exhausts what she means to him, changing the provocation.
RM-HF-D10D-F017.explanation: Kirei questions whether Sakura is worth Shirou's life. The English instead questions whether sacrifice exhausts what she means to him, changing the provocation.
RM-HF-D10D-F017.sourceReading: Having called life-sacrificing devotion beautiful, Kirei questions whether Sakura is worth that much to Shirou.

RM-HF-D10F-F003.description: Illya's sudden emergence from listlessness becomes a loss of enthusiasm. Her hostility toward Sakura is still visible, so the error primarily concerns Illya's changing mood.
RM-HF-D10F-F003.explanation: Illya's sudden emergence from listlessness becomes a loss of enthusiasm. Her hostility toward Sakura is still visible, so the error primarily concerns Illya's changing mood.
RM-HF-D10F-F003.sourceReading: Illya's immediately preceding listlessness abruptly disappears as she glares at Sakura.

RM-S0203-F013.description: “Getting there” loses Sakura's archery joke about bringing Shirou within range. Her ambition to surpass him and her confident challenge remain.
RM-S0203-F013.explanation: “Getting there” loses Sakura's archery joke about bringing Shirou within range. Her ambition to surpass him and her confident challenge remain.
RM-S0203-F013.sourceReading: Sakura playfully says Shirou's cooking is nearly within range, linking her cooking ambition to the archery hobby just mentioned.

RM-HF-D10F-F011.description: Thinking about how to save Sakura becomes postponing concern for himself. The surrounding English still establishes her urgent need for help.
RM-HF-D10F-F011.explanation: Thinking about how to save Sakura becomes postponing concern for himself. The surrounding English still establishes her urgent need for help.
RM-HF-D10F-F011.sourceReading: Shirou directs his present thinking toward how to defeat Zouken and obtain the Grail before Sakura collapses.

RM-S0210-F001.description: “Seemed down” makes Shirou's stated reason less clearly about physical illness. The surrounding English still describes Sakura as unwell.
RM-S0210-F001.explanation: “Seemed down” makes Shirou's stated reason less clearly about physical illness. The surrounding English still describes Sakura as unwell.
RM-S0210-F001.sourceReading: Shirou came because Sakura had appeared physically unwell since morning.

RM-R5A-F008.description: Sakura's formal announcement of reconciliation becomes an ordinary report of working things out. The midnight detail and her remaining discomfort with Saber survive.
RM-R5A-F008.explanation: Sakura's formal announcement of reconciliation becomes an ordinary report of working things out. The midnight detail and her remaining discomfort with Saber survive.
RM-R5A-F008.sourceReading: Sakura ceremoniously announces complete reconciliation effective at midnight.

RM-HF-D10G-F003.description: The English makes Sakura imagine injuring Shirou herself. The Japanese gives her a disturbing wish that he be injured, while leaving its cause unspecified.
RM-HF-D10G-F003.explanation: The English makes Sakura imagine injuring Shirou herself. The Japanese gives her a disturbing wish that he be injured, while leaving its cause unspecified.
RM-HF-D10G-F003.sourceReading: Sakura recalls wishing that Shirou would sustain an injury severe enough to keep him indoors. The thought does not specify who would cause it.

RM-S06A-F020.description: Sakura's explanation that she receives meals here becomes a promise to feed Shirou. Cleaning changes from reciprocating hospitality to another part of caring for him.
RM-S06A-F020.explanation: Sakura's explanation that she receives meals here becomes a promise to feed Shirou. Cleaning changes from reciprocating hospitality to another part of caring for him.
RM-S06A-F020.sourceReading: Sakura describes receiving hospitality: she spends mornings here and gets to eat dinner here, so cleaning is a reasonable contribution.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F011.description: The sentence needs 'put so much work into making.' Shirou's apology and appreciation remain clear.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F011.explanation: The sentence needs 'put so much work into making.' Shirou's apology and appreciation remain clear.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F011.sourceReading: Shirou apologizes because Taiga barely savored the breakfast Sakura prepared.

RM-S06F11A-F003.description: Shirou's meal as repayment for the morning porridge becomes porridge with an accompaniment, removing the stated return of care.
RM-S06F11A-F003.explanation: Shirou's meal as repayment for the morning porridge becomes porridge with an accompaniment, removing the stated return of care.
RM-S06F11A-F003.sourceReading: After putting the feverish Sakura to bed, Shirou must make something in return for the morning porridge.

RM-S13C-F014.description: The request loses 'first thing' after recovery. The promise to eat Sakura's cooking and her return to the kitchen remain.
RM-S13C-F014.explanation: The request loses 'first thing' after recovery. The promise to eat Sakura's cooking and her return to the kitchen remain.
RM-S13C-F014.sourceReading: Sakura asks him to give eating her cooking first priority once she recovers.

RM-S13B-F001.description: The bowl is no longer identified as having held porridge, making the trace of sickroom care less specific. Shirou still infers that he visited Sakura.
RM-S13B-F001.explanation: The bowl is no longer identified as having held porridge, making the trace of sickroom care less specific. Shirou still infers that he visited Sakura.
RM-S13B-F001.sourceReading: An emptied porridge dish, Sakura's pajamas, and a wet towel lead Shirou to infer that he visited her earlier.

RM-S0203-F009.description: Getting up at five becomes cooking 'so early.' The specific cost to Sakura's sleep is less concrete, while Shirou's concern remains.
RM-S0203-F009.explanation: Getting up at five becomes cooking 'so early.' The specific cost to Sakura's sleep is less concrete, while Shirou's concern remains.
RM-S0203-F009.sourceReading: Shirou thinks getting up at five to make a bento must be hard even for someone who enjoys cooking.

RM-R04F-F001.description: Taiga teases Shirou for preferring male friends to girls. The English reverses that preference, disconnecting her joke from his departure to find Issei.
RM-R04F-F001.explanation: Taiga teases Shirou for preferring male friends to girls. The English reverses that preference, disconnecting her joke from his departure to find Issei.
RM-R04F-F001.sourceReading: Taiga teases Shirou for choosing a male friend over girls as he leaves to look for Issei.

RM-R04D-F013.description: Shirou asks Sakura to fetch Taiga; the English asks her to deliver the lunch. The final handoff is not established here.
RM-R04D-F013.explanation: Shirou asks Sakura to fetch Taiga; the English asks her to deliver the lunch. The final handoff is not established here.
RM-R04D-F013.sourceReading: Shirou asks Sakura to bring Taiga over.

RM-R04H-F005.description: Sakura's braced determination becomes enthusiasm. The physical tension is lost, but these pages do not establish exactly what she is preparing herself for.
RM-R04H-F005.explanation: Sakura's braced determination becomes enthusiasm. The physical tension is lost, but these pages do not establish exactly what she is preparing herself for.
RM-R04H-F005.sourceReading: Shirou wonders why Sakura responds to the sleepover invitation with such tense, braced determination.

RM-R5C-F004.description: Sakura's regular preparation of his handkerchief becomes her supplying this one, leaving the recurring care unstated.
RM-R5C-F004.explanation: Sakura's regular preparation of his handkerchief becomes her supplying this one, leaving the recurring care unstated.
RM-R5C-F004.sourceReading: Shirou trusts the handkerchief's cleanliness because Sakura regularly prepares one for him.

RM-S06A-F015.description: Sakura's stated wish to nurse Shirou becomes a general wish to thank him. The surrounding scene still makes her caregiving role clear.
RM-S06A-F015.explanation: Sakura's stated wish to nurse Shirou becomes a general wish to thank him. The surrounding scene still makes her caregiving role clear.
RM-S06A-F015.sourceReading: Sakura clarifies that she wants to skip school because she wants to nurse Shirou, describing it hesitantly as thanks for yesterday.

RM-S06B-F009.description: Shirou's thought that Sakura is welcome to eat becomes a statement about her appetite, removing his reassurance that she need not hold back.
RM-S06B-F009.explanation: Shirou's thought that Sakura is welcome to eat becomes a statement about her appetite, removing his reassurance that she need not hold back.
RM-S06B-F009.sourceReading: Shirou thinks Sakura need not hold back: he has no objection to her eating the dorayaki.

RM-S06E-F003.description: Sakura's lowered face becomes her standing in Shirou's way. His ensuing question about her health loses its stated visual cue.
RM-S06E-F003.explanation: Sakura's lowered face becomes her standing in Shirou's way. His ensuing question about her health loses its stated visual cue.
RM-S06E-F003.sourceReading: Shirou notices that Sakura has lowered her face for some unexplained reason, then asks whether she feels unwell.

RM-S06F11A-F007.description: The offer loses its specific reason: Sakura may be wide awake after resting so much. Shirou still offers her companionship.
RM-S06F11A-F007.explanation: The offer loses its specific reason: Sakura may be wide awake after resting so much. Shirou still offers her companionship.
RM-S06F11A-F007.sourceReading: Shirou offers conversation if all her resting has left Sakura wide awake.

RM-S09F-F008.description: The expected benefit of fever medicine becomes waiting for the fever to break. His plans for a caretaker and a later hospital visit remain.
RM-S09F-F008.explanation: The expected benefit of fever medicine becomes waiting for the fever to break. His plans for a caretaker and a later hospital visit remain.
RM-S09F-F008.sourceReading: Shirou expects fever-reducing medicine alone to help Sakura recover enough for a later hospital visit.

RM-HF-D10G-F005.description: The Japanese says Shirou suffered an injury independently of Sakura’s wish. The English explicitly says she hurt him. This adds an agent to the clause without settling the wider cause of the injury.
RM-HF-D10G-F005.explanation: The Japanese says Shirou suffered an injury independently of Sakura’s wish. The English explicitly says she hurt him. This adds an agent to the clause without settling the wider cause of the injury.
RM-HF-D10G-F005.sourceReading: 彼女の願いとは関係なく separates the actual injury from her earlier wish; 衛宮士郎は傷を負った does not explicitly name Sakura as the actor who inflicted it.

RM-HF-D10F-C046.description: Rider explicitly protects Sakura by choice and affection, independently of Command Spell restraint.
RM-HF-D10F-C046.explanation: Rider explicitly protects Sakura by choice and affection, independently of Command Spell restraint.

RM-P2-001.description: The English describes the marks as bestowed upon summoning, omitting the Japanese distinction between an earlier Grail-given stigma and its transformation into a Master's mark.
RM-P2-001.explanation: The English describes the marks as bestowed upon summoning, omitting the Japanese distinction between an earlier Grail-given stigma and its transformation into a Master's mark.
RM-P2-001.sourceReading: A stigma supplied by the Grail changes through summoning into the Master's identifying mark. The ruby よちょう additionally presents the stigma as a precursor.

RM-R7K-004.description: A dull tingling becomes sharp, searing pain. The mark still loses its color in the following passage.
RM-R7K-004.explanation: A dull tingling becomes sharp, searing pain. The mark still loses its color in the following passage.
RM-R7K-004.sourceReading: A dull numbness or tingling passes across the back of Shirou's left hand and subsides, immediately before he notices the mark's lost color.

RM-S0317-F020.description: The supplied sentence needs 'run out of Command Spells.' Its meaning remains recoverable, so it does not support a claim that the expenditure rule changed.
RM-S0317-F020.explanation: The supplied sentence needs 'run out of Command Spells.' Its meaning remains recoverable, so it does not support a claim that the expenditure rule changed.
RM-S0317-F020.sourceReading: Rin warns about what will happen once Shirou has no Command Spells left.

RM-R7M-004.description: This branch repeats the change from dull tingling to sharp, searing pain. The following description of the fading mark remains intact.
RM-R7M-004.explanation: This branch repeats the change from dull tingling to sharp, searing pain. The following description of the fading mark remains intact.
RM-R7M-004.sourceReading: A dull numbness or tingling briefly crosses Shirou's hand before he notices the Command Spell's color fading.

RM-S0408B-F011.description: Saber's objection loses 'only three,' removing her explicit reminder that Shirou would be spending a scarce command on preventing her from protecting him.
RM-S0408B-F011.explanation: Saber's objection loses 'only three,' removing her explicit reminder that Shirou would be spending a scarce command on preventing her from protecting him.
RM-S0408B-F011.sourceReading: Saber objects both to the self-defeating order and to spending a command entitlement from a stock of only three.

RM-S0610-F002.description: The Command Spells' apparent warning becomes a warning from the wind, and something about to happen overhead becomes something already happening.
RM-S0610-F002.explanation: The Command Spells' apparent warning becomes a warning from the wind, and something about to happen overhead becomes something already happening.
RM-S0610-F002.sourceReading: The fragment qualifies the preceding statement that the Command Spells ache: they seem to issue a warning about the roaring wind and something about to happen overhead.

RM-S1000B-F015.description: Making Shinji use a Command Spell becomes making him use up his supply. The Japanese leaves the count and intended order unstated and expects the need to fight Rider to end.
RM-S1000B-F015.explanation: Making Shinji use a Command Spell becomes making him use up his supply. The Japanese leaves the count and intended order unstated and expects the need to fight Rider to end.
RM-S1000B-F015.sourceReading: Shirou expects that finding Shinji and making him use a Command Spell will remove the need to fight Rider. Neither the remaining count nor the intended order is specified.

RM-S1517B-F011.description: A restriction on who can perform the transfer becomes a restriction on whom it occurs between. This changes the stated role of Masters and Servants in transplantation.
RM-S1517B-F011.explanation: A restriction on who can perform the transfer becomes a restriction on whom it occurs between. This changes the stated role of Masters and Servants in transplantation.
RM-S1517B-F011.sourceReading: Only a Master or a Servant can perform the transplantation of Command Spells.

RM-S08C-F040.description: The English omits the final surge of pain before the marks disappear. It preserves their disappearance and the following explanation that Shirou has lost his qualification as a Master.
RM-S08C-F040.explanation: The English omits the final surge of pain before the marks disappear. It preserves their disappearance and the following explanation that Shirou has lost his qualification as a Master.
RM-S08C-F040.sourceReading: Shirou's left hand hurts especially strongly before the disappearance. The following sentences explicitly identify the Command Spells as disappearing; the immediate subject of 消えた need not be forced.

RM-R12A-F012.description: Archer's warning that he could be compelled to attack Caster becomes a warning that Rin will attack her. This obscures why breaking Archer's contract is urgent.
RM-R12A-F012.explanation: Archer's warning that he could be compelled to attack Caster becomes a warning that Rin will attack her. This obscures why breaking Archer's contract is urgent.
RM-R12A-F012.sourceReading: Archer urges Caster to break his contract before Rin can use her remaining Command Spell to make him attack Caster.

RM-S0411B-F013.description: Shirou's vague report changes from the middle of Rin's right arm to the middle of her right hand. This concerns his reported location, not proof of where her mark actually lies.
RM-S0411B-F013.explanation: Shirou's vague report changes from the middle of Rin's right arm to the middle of her right hand. This concerns his reported location, not proof of where her mark actually lies.
RM-S0411B-F013.sourceReading: Shirou vaguely reports that Rin's mark is somewhere around the middle of her right arm, on the opposite side from his.

RM-S0610-F010.description: The English makes the Master's awareness explicitly immediate. These lines do not identify Command Spells as the means of transmission, so they cannot establish a change to their behavior.
RM-S0610-F010.explanation: The English makes the Master's awareness explicitly immediate. These lines do not identify Command Spells as the means of transmission, so they cannot establish a change to their behavior.
RM-S0610-F010.sourceReading: Rin says Saber's independent attack was highly likely and that a Master becomes aware when a Servant starts fighting.

RM-P2-004.description: The Japanese says powerful mages are easier to detect; the English says they are better at detecting others. This reverses the sensing relation behind Rin's observation about the town.
RM-P2-004.explanation: The Japanese says powerful mages are easier to detect; the English says they are better at detecting others. This reverses the sensing relation behind Rin's observation about the town.
RM-P2-004.sourceReading: A mage carrying powerful magical energy is correspondingly easy to detect. Rin then says she knows of nobody with that much energy in town.

RM-R04J-F003.description: Saber's alternative descriptions—renown or an extraordinary feat—become two affirmative descriptions of the same group. The passage does not establish a formal two-part eligibility rule.
RM-R04J-F003.explanation: Saber's alternative descriptions—renown or an extraordinary feat—become two affirmative descriptions of the same group. The passage does not establish a formal two-part eligibility rule.
RM-R04J-F003.sourceReading: Saber describes Heroic Spirits as people who became renowned in their own eras or accomplished feats beyond human capacity.

RM-S0317-F027.description: The English adds that the attacking Servant must be in spirit form. Rin's Japanese identifies Servants as fellow spiritual beings; her following exception concerns a target that has materialized.
RM-S0317-F027.explanation: The English adds that the attacking Servant must be in spirit form. Rin's Japanese identifies Servants as fellow spiritual beings; her following exception concerns a target that has materialized.
RM-S0317-F027.sourceReading: Rin identifies fellow spiritual beings, Servants, as the opponents capable of defeating Servants, then allows that humans might defeat a materialized one.

RM-S08B-F003.description: Rider's intimidating presence becomes physical prowess. Her superiority to Assassin remains, but the English changes what the narrator observes as evidence of it.
RM-S08B-F003.explanation: Rider's intimidating presence becomes physical prowess. Her superiority to Assassin remains, but the English changes what the narrator observes as evidence of it.
RM-S08B-F003.sourceReading: Rider's magical energy and the intimidating force of her presence are markedly greater than before.

RM-S0401B-F011.description: Shirou's account of invisible spirits affecting the world as if embodied becomes an account of interaction after materialization. The following description of invisible killers makes that change consequential within his reasoning.
RM-S0401B-F011.explanation: Shirou's account of invisible spirits affecting the world as if embodied becomes an account of interaction after materialization. The following description of invisible killers makes that change consequential within his reasoning.
RM-S0401B-F011.sourceReading: Shirou reasons that unseen spiritual beings can nevertheless affect the world as though they possessed physical bodies.

RM-S08B-F017.description: Saber's reference to an entity classifiable as neither Master nor Servant becomes a question about ignoring other participants. The previous page preserves the classification uncertainty, so the loss is local to her stated objection.
RM-S08B-F017.explanation: Saber's reference to an entity classifiable as neither Master nor Servant becomes a question about ignoring other participants. The previous page preserves the classification uncertainty, so the loss is local to her stated objection.
RM-S08B-F017.sourceReading: Saber questions engaging something that cannot be identified as either Master or Servant and appears unrelated to their objective.

RM-R14A-F017.description: A comparison between these two combatants becomes a rule about Archer- and Saber-class Servants. Archer's later description of himself likewise becomes a claim about all archers' preferences; the dialogue may be rhetorical, but its scope is broader.
RM-R14A-F017.explanation: A comparison between these two combatants becomes a rule about Archer- and Saber-class Servants. Archer's later description of himself likewise becomes a claim about all archers' preferences; the dialogue may be rhetorical, but its scope is broader.
RM-R14A-F017.sourceReading: The narration compares the two fighters just shown struggling unequally. Later, Archer invokes his designation to explain that he is not fundamentally a sword fighter.

RM-S0404B-F005.description: Rin's comparison with past Servants expands to all heroes of myth and legend. It remains her tentative assessment of close-combat strength.
RM-S0404B-F005.explanation: Rin's comparison with past Servants expands to all heroes of myth and legend. It remains her tentative assessment of close-combat strength.
RM-S0404B-F005.sourceReading: Rin thinks Berserker has no equal even among Servants of previous generations, within her close-combat comparison.

RM-S08C-F023.description: Saber's condition—face Assassin alone or expose the Master to the first attack—becomes a statement of Assassin's preference. Her protective purpose remains clear from the door and surrounding warnings.
RM-S08C-F023.explanation: Saber's condition—face Assassin alone or expose the Master to the first attack—becomes a statement of Assassin's preference. Her protective purpose remains clear from the door and surrounding warnings.
RM-S08C-F023.sourceReading: Saber says that unless she faces Assassin one-on-one, the Master will be attacked first.

RM-S08C-F027.description: An ominous presence around Assassin becomes an aura explicitly coming from him. The Japanese leaves its source unspecified, consistent with the next warning about the darkness ahead.
RM-S08C-F027.explanation: An ominous presence around Assassin becomes an aura explicitly coming from him. The Japanese leaves its source unspecified, consistent with the next warning about the darkness ahead.
RM-S08C-F027.sourceReading: Saber senses something ominous around Assassin, without identifying him as its source. The next page warns against approaching the darkness.

RM-S0408B-F015.description: A rare ability to jump across space becomes travel through space and time. The passage discusses reaching a distant Master, and supplies no temporal component.
RM-S0408B-F015.explanation: A rare ability to jump across space becomes travel through space and time. The passage discusses reaching a distant Master, and supplies no temporal component.
RM-S0408B-F015.sourceReading: Jumping across space would overcome the problem of reaching Shirou from far away; few Servants possess that ability.

RM-S09G-F021.description: The Japanese explains that intimidating pressure scales with sensed magical energy. The English instead says magical energy causes skin-crawling, losing the relation behind Shirou's comparison of Rider's strength.
RM-S09G-F021.explanation: The Japanese explains that intimidating pressure scales with sensed magical energy. The English instead says magical energy causes skin-crawling, losing the relation behind Shirou's comparison of Rider's strength.
RM-S09G-F021.sourceReading: A Servant's intimidating presence varies in proportion to the magical energy perceptible through bodily sensation, supporting Shirou's assessment that Rider has changed.

RM-S0411B-F019.description: The English preserves variation between wars but omits Rin's approximate scale of one or two changed classes. The current basic lineup and the following warning about individual abilities remain.
RM-S0411B-F019.explanation: The English preserves variation between wars but omits Rin's approximate scale of one or two changed classes. The current basic lineup and the following warning about individual abilities remain.
RM-S0411B-F019.sourceReading: Rin reports that apparently one or two classes change from war to war, before identifying the present lineup as basic.

RM-S13B-F004.description: An explicit reminder that Assassin already crossed the barrier becomes a statement that he might be able to do so. The preceding reference to that morning survives, but the event itself is no longer stated.
RM-S13B-F004.explanation: An explicit reminder that Assassin already crossed the barrier becomes a statement that he might be able to do so. The preceding reference to that morning survives, but the event itself is no longer stated.
RM-S13B-F004.sourceReading: Shirou recalls Assassin having already passed the house's Bounded Field without difficulty that morning.

RM-S1000B-F006.description: Shirou's ability to express observed Servant capabilities numerically becomes merely some understanding of Rider's abilities. The passage does not specify a display or particular numerical values.
RM-S1000B-F006.explanation: Shirou's ability to express observed Servant capabilities numerically becomes merely some understanding of Rider's abilities. The passage does not specify a display or particular numerical values.
RM-S1000B-F006.sourceReading: After seeing a Servant fight, Shirou can quantify its abilities even when it belongs to another Master. He is uncertain whether the contract or Command Spells enable this.

RM-S1003B-F008.description: “Phantasmal” names both the broad group and the higher level this Pegasus has attained. The Japanese distinguishes those terms, so the English obscures the intermediate classification while preserving the approach to dragon-level strength.
RM-S1003B-F008.explanation: “Phantasmal” names both the broad group and the higher level this Pegasus has attained. The Japanese distinguishes those terms, so the English obscures the intermediate classification while preserving the approach to dragon-level strength.
RM-S1003B-F008.sourceReading: An ordinary Pegasus belongs to the Demonic Beast class within Phantasmal Species. This ancient individual has reached the distinct Phantasmal Beast level and approaches dragons.

RM-S1118-F003.description: Shirou's “if Masters can tell” becomes a declarative statement that they can. His conclusion about Archer remains supported by Rin's behavior and response; the change concerns his certainty about the mechanism.
RM-S1118-F003.explanation: Shirou's “if Masters can tell” becomes a declarative statement that they can. His conclusion about Archer remains supported by Rin's behavior and response; the change concerns his certainty about the mechanism.
RM-S1118-F003.sourceReading: Shirou reasons conditionally: if Masters can sense a Servant's life or death as Saber sensed his danger, Rin's gesture has a particular meaning.

RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F024.description: 'Major businessman' replaces the specific fact that Fujimura is a major landowner. This belongs in a dossier on local background or property, rather than Taiga's characterization.
RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F024.explanation: 'Major businessman' replaces the specific fact that Fujimura is a major landowner. This belongs in a dossier on local background or property, rather than Taiga's characterization.
RM-FATE-D1-OPENING-F024.sourceReading: Shirou identifies Old Man Fujimura as a major local landowner after explaining his help with property administration.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F012.description: Shinto becomes a neighboring city even though the supplied overview identifies it as the modern half of Fuyuki.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F012.explanation: Shinto becomes a neighboring city even though the supplied overview identifies it as the modern half of Fuyuki.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F012.sourceReading: The accident occurs in neighboring Shinto. The supplied prologue explicitly identifies Shinto and Miyama as parts of Fuyuki City.

RM-S15F-F014.description: The English retains the land's exceptional quality but drops its stated position below Aozaki's territory.
RM-S15F-F014.explanation: The English retains the land's exceptional quality but drops its stated position below Aozaki's territory.
RM-S15F-F014.sourceReading: The land is first-rate, ranking after the territory administered by Aozaki.

RM-S0200-F006.description: A general rule that such land always has an established mage becomes a guess about Fuyuki. The following explanation still preserves the Second Owner's territorial authority.
RM-S0200-F006.explanation: A general rule that such land always has an established mage becomes a guess about Fuyuki. The following explanation still preserves the Second Owner's territorial authority.
RM-S0200-F006.sourceReading: Shirou states a general rule that spiritually superior land invariably has an established prestigious mage occupying it.

RM-S15J-F007.description: The circuit's resemblance to a huge rotating observatory becomes a view of Arizona through a telescope, changing the image used to describe the ritual structure.
RM-S15J-F007.explanation: The circuit's resemblance to a huge rotating observatory becomes a view of Arizona through a telescope, changing the image used to describe the ritual structure.
RM-S15J-F007.sourceReading: The enormous circuit resembles an enormous observation apparatus rotating alone in the Arizona wilderness.

RM-S0204-F002.description: The comparison with the burned ground's immediate surroundings becomes a general comparison with maintained places. The English need not describe the entire park as neglected.
RM-S0204-F002.explanation: The comparison with the burned ground's immediate surroundings becomes a general comparison with maintained places. The English need not describe the entire park as neglected.
RM-S0204-F002.sourceReading: The neglected ground looks shabby beside its properly leveled surroundings. The following page distinguishes this ground from the park it could enlarge.

RM-HF-D4-CHURCH-PATROL-F001.description: Kirei's dismissal of racial classification becomes praise for excellence surviving mixed ancestry, adding an ancestry claim and reversing the force of his qualification.
RM-HF-D4-CHURCH-PATROL-F001.explanation: Kirei's dismissal of racial classification becomes praise for excellence surviving mixed ancestry, adding an ancestry claim and reversing the force of his qualification.
RM-HF-D4-CHURCH-PATROL-F001.sourceReading: Kirei says racial classification would be ridiculous if the Tohsakas' grandmaster is as reported. The passage identifies a grandmaster relationship, not biological descent from him.

RM-S0606B-F005.description: The route loses its specified destination partway up the mountain; the English gives only a general mountain approach.
RM-S0606B-F005.explanation: The route loses its specified destination partway up the mountain; the English gives only a general mountain approach.
RM-S0606B-F005.sourceReading: The route leads partway up the mountain, toward the temple identified on the preceding page.

RM-S0612-F004.description: Rin's father's report of something resembling a leyline becomes a report that Fuyuki has one. The attribution remains, but the uncertainty about identification disappears.
RM-S0612-F004.explanation: Rin's father's report of something resembling a leyline becomes a report that Fuyuki has one. The attribution remains, but the uncertainty about identification disappears.
RM-S0612-F004.sourceReading: Rin recalls her father mentioning something resembling a dragon vein or leyline.

RM-S1100-F003.description: The inscription names Britain in Japanese and England in English. Its royal-selection function remains, but the named realm changes.
RM-S1100-F003.explanation: The inscription names Britain in Japanese and England in English. Its royal-selection function remains, but the named realm changes.
RM-S1100-F003.sourceReading: The inscription identifies the successful sword-puller as the person entitled to rule Britain.

RM-S1517B-F004.description: The cleared summit's completely flat surface becomes a smoldering wasteland. The English adds burning and drops the stated shape of the remaining ground.
RM-S1517B-F004.explanation: The cleared summit's completely flat surface becomes a smoldering wasteland. The English adds burning and drops the stated shape of the remaining ground.
RM-S1517B-F004.sourceReading: Everything on the summit has been blown away, leaving a completely flat wasteland.

RM-S15F-F016.description: Unused mana outside the world becomes mana in 'this land,' and its abundance becomes the reason it has not been used. This blurs the distinction between the Grail's external reward and Fuyuki's slowly collected local supply.
RM-S15F-F016.explanation: Unused mana outside the world becomes mana in 'this land,' and its abundance becomes the reason it has not been used. This blurs the distinction between the Grail's external reward and Fuyuki's slowly collected local supply.
RM-S15F-F016.sourceReading: The outside contains unused mana in quantities incomparable with those on earth; this explains the immense energy available through the Grail.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F016.description: Passing the wall before emerging onto the descent becomes walking downhill alongside it. The broader route into the residential area remains intact.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F016.explanation: Passing the wall before emerging onto the descent becomes walking downhill alongside it. The broader route into the residential area remains intact.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F016.sourceReading: They pass the long wall, emerge onto the downhill stretch, and then reach the populated residential area.

RM-P1-015.description: The cemetery's actual restriction to immigrant-generation graves becomes its original purpose, making the observation about later generations less explicit.
RM-P1-015.explanation: The cemetery's actual restriction to immigrant-generation graves becomes its original purpose, making the observation about later generations less explicit.
RM-P1-015.sourceReading: Only members of the immigrant generation have graves there, supporting Rin's observation that foreigners are now absent.

RM-P2-005.description: Miyama's preserved old streetscape becomes a claim that Fuyuki grew from a village, adding settlement history absent from the passage.
RM-P2-005.explanation: Miyama's preserved old streetscape becomes a claim that Fuyuki grew from a village, adding settlement history absent from the passage.
RM-P2-005.sourceReading: Miyama retains its old streetscape, in contrast with modern development across the river.

RM-P3-002.description: Rin's identification of her homeroom teacher becomes an assignment for her class. This belongs in a review of school relationships.
RM-P3-002.explanation: Rin's identification of her homeroom teacher becomes an assignment for her class. This belongs in a review of school relationships.
RM-P3-002.sourceReading: Rin recognizes World History as the subject taught by her homeroom teacher, Kuzuki.

RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F011.description: Rin's reason for explaining Magic Crests becomes an assertion that Shirou already understands them. The Japanese says learning about crests will explain what being a mage means.
RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F011.explanation: Rin's reason for explaining Magic Crests becomes an assertion that Shirou already understands them. The Japanese says learning about crests will explain what being a mage means.
RM-FATE-D7-LESSON-F011.sourceReading: Understanding Magic Crests means understanding what a mage is; this explains why Rin will teach the subject from the beginning.

RM-S12D-F013.description: An existing lookalike object reinforced through Projection becomes a Projection supplemented by more magecraft. This changes the method being contrasted with Shirou's complete mental construction.
RM-S12D-F013.explanation: An existing lookalike object reinforced through Projection becomes a Projection supplemented by more magecraft. This changes the method being contrasted with Shirou's complete mental construction.
RM-S12D-F013.sourceReading: Ordinary Projection can be layered onto an object resembling the original to reinforce it. Shirou instead must construct everything through his own mental image.

RM-R04D-F001.description: Two problems Shirou attributes to his inexperience become a causal chain in which his missing energy supply prevents Saber from taking spirit form. This changes his account of their dependence, without establishing the actual cause beyond this passage.
RM-R04D-F001.explanation: Two problems Shirou attributes to his inexperience become a causal chain in which his missing energy supply prevents Saber from taking spirit form. This changes his account of their dependence, without establishing the actual cause beyond this passage.
RM-R04D-F001.sourceReading: Shirou reports two deficiencies: Saber cannot become a spirit, and she receives none of the energy normally supplied by a Master. He attributes both to his inexperience.

RM-HF-D10A-F008.description: Sakura's warning about accidental exposure becomes a warning that Rider might attack on impulse. Rider's next lines still explain that she cannot reliably prevent her eyes from affecting Shirou.
RM-HF-D10A-F008.explanation: Sakura's warning about accidental exposure becomes a warning that Rider might attack on impulse. Rider's next lines still explain that she cannot reliably prevent her eyes from affecting Shirou.
RM-HF-D10A-F008.sourceReading: Sakura warns that Shirou might inadvertently fall under the eyes' effect. Rider explains that even limiting her magical energy would not reliably exclude him.

RM-R04E-F002.description: The English introduces mentally hitting targets during magecraft practice. The Japanese only says that nightly training enables Shirou to make his arrows strike as imagined.
RM-R04E-F002.explanation: The English introduces mentally hitting targets during magecraft practice. The Japanese only says that nightly training enables Shirou to make his arrows strike as imagined.
RM-R04E-F002.sourceReading: Shirou credits his nightly magecraft training with enabling arrows to strike as he imagines, explaining why he expects to retain his former archery results.

RM-S1207B-F009.description: Rin's explanation of passing energy into objects becomes passing it through oneself. The English also drops her distinction between energy used as material and energy used to initiate an effect on nature.
RM-S1207B-F009.explanation: Rin's explanation of passing energy into objects becomes passing it through oneself. The English also drops her distinction between energy used as material and energy used to initiate an effect on nature.
RM-S1207B-F009.sourceReading: Rin explains using energy through objects or using it as a starter for interference with nature, in contrast with treating free-standing energy as durable material.

RM-HF-D10H-F002.description: The English preserves the ruby's name but loses the treasure chest and Illya's expectation that it will be beautiful. 'Sounds pretty nice' need not mean she likes the sound of the name.
RM-HF-D10H-F002.explanation: The English preserves the ruby's name but loses the treasure chest and Illya's expectation that it will be beautiful. 'Sounds pretty nice' need not mean she likes the sound of the name.
RM-HF-D10H-F002.sourceReading: Illya expresses interest in the apparent beauty of a treasure chest used by a magician, with a proper name supplied through ruby.

RM-HF-D14B-F023.description: The English dates implantation to the last war. The Japanese dates the leakage to that war and leaves the implantation date unstated.
RM-HF-D14B-F023.explanation: The English dates implantation to the last war. The Japanese dates the leakage to that war and leaves the implantation date unstated.
RM-HF-D14B-F023.sourceReading: The previous war dates the leakage of what was subsequently implanted in Sakura. The sentence does not independently date implantation.

RM-R11D-F006.description: Caster's appraisal of Rin's magecraft becomes an appraisal of her ability as a Master, blurring the technical comparison that explains Caster's preference for Shirou.
RM-R11D-F006.explanation: Caster's appraisal of Rin's magecraft becomes an appraisal of her ability as a Master, blurring the technical comparison that explains Caster's preference for Shirou.
RM-R11D-F006.sourceReading: Caster acknowledges Rin's proficiency as a mage, places it below her own, and contrasts it with Shirou's immature but distinctive and exploitable ability.

RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F003.description: The first occurrence of 'user of magecraft' becomes 'mage,' weakening its connection to Kiritsugu's later distinction. The English does preserve that distinction when Kiritsugu explains it explicitly.
RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F003.explanation: The first occurrence of 'user of magecraft' becomes 'mage,' weakening its connection to Kiritsugu's later distinction. The English does preserve that distinction when Kiritsugu explains it explicitly.
RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F003.sourceReading: Connecting the circuit makes Shirou a practitioner of magecraft. Later, Kiritsugu expressly distinguishes that status from being a mage through the purpose for which he uses it.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F021.description: Zouken's account of sending Sakura to another family becomes an account of the Matous adopting someone. The stated obstacle also changes from the prospective adoptee's lack of circuits to the family's lack of circuits to pass on.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F021.explanation: Zouken's account of sending Sakura to another family becomes an account of the Matous adopting someone. The stated obstacle also changes from the prospective adoptee's lack of circuits to the family's lack of circuits to pass on.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F021.sourceReading: Zouken says the unselected sibling could have been sent out for adoption, but no receiving family would want someone without circuits. The surrounding questions identify Sakura as the person under discussion.

RM-R13C-F003.description: A family creation perfected as a Magic Circuit becomes someone who inherited circuits perfected over generations. The English adds an inheritance mechanism and changes what was perfected.
RM-R13C-F003.explanation: A family creation perfected as a Magic Circuit becomes someone who inherited circuits perfected over generations. The English adds an inheritance mechanism and changes what was perfected.
RM-R13C-F003.sourceReading: The family's creation has been perfected as a Magic Circuit; it is this creation that they believe can accomplish their aim.

RM-P1-055.description: The Japanese makes Rin's human body resist its own circuit state. The English makes the stigmata reject her body, changing the source of the resistance.
RM-P1-055.explanation: The Japanese makes Rin's human body resist its own circuit state. The English makes the stigmata reject her body, changing the source of the resistance.
RM-P1-055.sourceReading: Rin's human body rejects that same body in its circuit state; the stigmata express this conflict.

RM-R04E-F012.description: Becoming a circuit changes to making a circuit. This loses the explicit identification of practitioner and conduit, although the surrounding discussion still preserves self-erasure.
RM-R04E-F012.explanation: Becoming a circuit changes to making a circuit. This loses the explicit identification of practitioner and conduit, although the surrounding discussion still preserves self-erasure.
RM-R04E-F012.sourceReading: The practitioner suppresses the self and becomes a circuit, paralleling the self-emptying discipline of archery.

RM-S06A-F007.description: A breaker about to trip becomes one that trips. The change makes the metaphorical interruption more definite; it does not establish a literal bodily shutdown.
RM-S06A-F007.explanation: A breaker about to trip becomes one that trips. The change makes the metaphorical interruption more definite; it does not establish a literal bodily shutdown.
RM-S06A-F007.sourceReading: Trying to think about the dream brings him close to a protective shutdown, expressed through a breaker metaphor.

RM-R10H-F001.description: Releasing a sensation becomes removing a nerve. The English makes the description more concrete, though the magical context does not require literal anatomical extraction.
RM-R10H-F001.explanation: Releasing a sensation becomes removing a nerve. The English makes the description more concrete, though the magical context does not require literal anatomical extraction.
RM-R10H-F001.sourceReading: Shirou disengages the sensation embedded in his spine, after which circuit-related tension releases.

RM-S0206-F007.description: Disturbed thinking under physical fatigue becomes distraction caused by the whole list of bodily effects. The English also supplies a circuit-causes-effects explanation that the compressed Japanese does not explicitly give.
RM-S0206-F007.explanation: Disturbed thinking under physical fatigue becomes distraction caused by the whole list of bodily effects. The English also supplies a circuit-causes-effects explanation that the compressed Japanese does not explicitly give.
RM-S0206-F007.sourceReading: During exercise, Shirou monitors internal processes, including disturbances in thought under bodily fatigue. The dash compresses their relation to Magic Circuits.

RM-S11F-F015.description: The English omits the gallbladder from the organ list. The surrounding account of extensive internal injury remains.
RM-S11F-F015.explanation: The English omits the gallbladder from the organ list. The surrounding account of extensive internal injury remains.
RM-S11F-F015.sourceReading: The compressed bodily inventory explicitly includes the gallbladder after the liver.

RM-S0307-F003.description: The first impression that his body below the chest is gone becomes a central hole. This changes the disoriented perception, without proving a different literal injury.
RM-S0307-F003.explanation: The first impression that his body below the chest is gone becomes a central hole. This changes the disoriented perception, without proving a different literal injury.
RM-S0307-F003.sourceReading: Shirou initially perceives his body below the chest as absent; the next page describes a large part of his abdomen being taken away.

RM-S16A-F007.description: An act that seems capable of shredding her nerves becomes one that does shred them. The English removes the qualification while preserving her cool demeanor.
RM-S16A-F007.explanation: An act that seems capable of shredding her nerves becomes one that does shred them. The English removes the qualification while preserving her cool demeanor.
RM-S16A-F007.sourceReading: Sakura performs an act that seems liable to shred the nerves throughout her body, while remaining outwardly cool.

RM-R14AA-F002.description: Structures running along Shinji's skin become muscles rippling beneath it. The English adds movement and a more specific anatomical location.
RM-R14AA-F002.explanation: Structures running along Shinji's skin become muscles rippling beneath it. The English adds movement and a more specific anatomical location.
RM-R14AA-F002.sourceReading: Ugly streaks or cordlike structures run along Shinji's skin and connect his body to the flesh mass.

RM-S0312-F005.description: Preserved outward appearance becomes preserved flesh and bones. This changes the hypothetical victim from a body whose contents are replaced into one whose tissues partly remain.
RM-S0312-F005.explanation: Preserved outward appearance becomes preserved flesh and bones. This changes the hypothetical victim from a body whose contents are replaced into one whose tissues partly remain.
RM-S0312-F005.sourceReading: An ordinary victim would retain its outward appearance while its contents were comprehensively replaced by worms.

RM-R14Y-F004.description: An unspecified giant organ becomes an intestine. The bodily comparison survives, but its anatomy is made more specific.
RM-R14Y-F004.explanation: An unspecified giant organ becomes an intestine. The bodily comparison survives, but its anatomy is made more specific.
RM-R14Y-F004.sourceReading: The mountain's raw vitality creates the impression of climbing an enormous, unspecified internal organ.

RM-S0909-F004.description: Internal organs being damaged becomes bones and organs being violently shaken. Serious injury remains clear, but the organ-specific impairment is less explicit.
RM-S0909-F004.explanation: Internal organs being damaged becomes bones and organs being violently shaken. Serious injury remains clear, but the organ-specific impairment is less explicit.
RM-S0909-F004.sourceReading: Shirou describes his internal organs as broadly damaged or put out of action by the impact, then separately estimates rib fractures.

RM-S1307B-F020.description: His body becoming a mere thing becomes his body stiffening. The death scene remains, but its explicit loss of personhood is replaced by a physical symptom.
RM-S1307B-F020.explanation: His body becoming a mere thing becomes his body stiffening. The death scene remains, but its explicit loss of personhood is replaced by a physical symptom.
RM-S1307B-F020.sourceReading: As Shirou dies, his body becomes a mere thing, expressing the loss of its living, personal status.

RM-S1400B-F022.description: Vital material spilling out of the wound becomes organs shifting inside him. This changes both the bodily event and the source's deliberately indistinct description.
RM-S1400B-F022.explanation: Vital material spilling out of the wound becomes organs shifting inside him. This changes both the bodily event and the source's deliberately indistinct description.
RM-S1400B-F022.sourceReading: Each exertion makes substantial amounts of something necessary for life spill from the wound; the material remains unnamed.

RM-S1500B-F014.description: Writhing sensations in his limbs become moving limbs that threaten to wrench out every nerve. The English changes the perceived event and broadens its anatomical scope.
RM-S1500B-F014.explanation: Writhing sensations in his limbs become moving limbs that threaten to wrench out every nerve. The English changes the perceived event and broadens its anatomical scope.
RM-S1500B-F014.sourceReading: Despite numbness, sensations in Shirou's limbs writhe as though about to shatter, while his heart continues beating.

RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F004.description: The single circuit's poker-like, intangible form becomes a series of metal rods. The English retains qualified invisibility, so the problem is added multiplicity and concreteness rather than straightforward visibility.
RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F004.explanation: The single circuit's poker-like, intangible form becomes a series of metal rods. The English retains qualified invisibility, so the problem is added multiplicity and concreteness rather than straightforward visibility.
RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F004.sourceReading: The preceding single circuit is described as an invisible, untouchable thing resembling a fire poker or tongs. Its insertion is expressly not merely metaphorical.

RM-S0312-F011.description: The English drops the specific description of the prepared being as a cellular implement. Its treatment as a manufactured, disposable thing remains clear nearby.
RM-S0312-F011.explanation: The English drops the specific description of the prepared being as a cellular implement. Its treatment as a manufactured, disposable thing remains clear nearby.
RM-S0312-F011.sourceReading: The prepared entity is called a cellular implement, with Grail fragments having invaded its nerves over ten years.

RM-P3-017.description: The injured person's inability to heal himself becomes Rin's inability to heal her own wounds. The allegation's identification of that person as Archer is unsupported here.
RM-P3-017.explanation: The injured person's inability to heal himself becomes Rin's inability to heal her own wounds. The allegation's identification of that person as Archer is unsupported here.
RM-P3-017.sourceReading: The injured person cannot heal himself; Rin separately says she lacks sufficient power to save him.

RM-S07G-F011.description: Rin's report that the strange entity vanished becomes a report that Shirou vanished. The Japanese exchange concerns what happened to the entity after he collapsed.
RM-S07G-F011.explanation: Rin's report that the strange entity vanished becomes a report that Shirou vanished. The Japanese exchange concerns what happened to the entity after he collapsed.
RM-S07G-F011.sourceReading: Answering Shirou's question about the strange entity, Rin says it disappeared as he stood on its shadow and collapsed.

RM-S13B-F012.description: An eruption compared more to an explosion than to water becomes a geyser of water. The violent image survives, but the source's contrast disappears.
RM-S13B-F012.explanation: An eruption compared more to an explosion than to water becomes a geyser of water. The violent image survives, but the source's contrast disappears.
RM-S13B-F012.sourceReading: The red eruption suggests an explosion more than a discharge of water.

RM-HF-D10I-F003.description: “Lady” removes the familiar older-sister address from the strange voice’s reply. The abnormal delivery remains, but the childlike familiarity changes.
RM-HF-D10I-F003.explanation: “Lady” removes the familiar older-sister address from the strange voice’s reply. The abnormal delivery remains, but the childlike familiarity changes.
RM-HF-D10I-F003.sourceReading: The strange voice answers Taiga’s identification question affirmatively, addressing her with the childlike, familiar オネエチャン.

RM-R12A-F007.description: “King Colchis” presents the realm as a personal name. The local lineage and identification of Medea nevertheless remain intact.
RM-R12A-F007.explanation: “King Colchis” presents the realm as a personal name. The local lineage and identification of Medea nevertheless remain intact.
RM-R12A-F007.sourceReading: The phrase attributes the magecraft to the king of Colchis, whose daughter is then identified as Medea.

RM-S0408B-F006.description: Their belated recognition that Rin has already been using “Shirou” for a while becomes agreement that she switched quickly.
RM-S0408B-F006.explanation: Their belated recognition that Rin has already been using “Shirou” for a while becomes agreement that she switched quickly.
RM-S0408B-F006.sourceReading: Rin suggests she has been using his given name for some time without noticing; Shirou agrees retrospectively.

RM-S0410B-F008.description: Shirou’s complaint follows both Rin and Saber repeatedly saying his name. “She” redirects the complaint toward a single woman, although their individual addresses remain in the dialogue.
RM-S0410B-F008.explanation: Shirou’s complaint follows both Rin and Saber repeatedly saying his name. “She” redirects the complaint toward a single woman, although their individual addresses remain in the dialogue.
RM-S0410B-F008.sourceReading: After Rin and Saber repeatedly use their respective 士郎 and シロウ forms, Shirou complains about being addressed so familiarly and repeatedly, like a found cat.

RM-S11B-F012.description: The English assigns Sakura’s blush to Tohsaka, who is next door, and changes Sakura’s murmuring into uneasy glances.
RM-S11B-F012.explanation: The English assigns Sakura’s blush to Tohsaka, who is next door, and changes Sakura’s murmuring into uneasy glances.
RM-S11B-F012.sourceReading: Sakura blushes and murmurs her reply to Shirou; Rin is in the adjacent room.

RM-R13D-F001.description: Rin’s reassurance uses “Shirou” in Japanese and “Emiya” in English. The comfort remains, but her chosen form of address changes.
RM-R13D-F001.explanation: Rin’s reassurance uses “Shirou” in Japanese and “Emiya” in English. The comfort remains, but her chosen form of address changes.
RM-R13D-F001.sourceReading: Rin uses Shirou’s given name while telling him he is not responsible for the girl’s death.

RM-R14A-F015.description: The same sword is called “Kanshou” and later “Kashou.” This is a small name-spelling inconsistency; the other two misspellings concern ordinary words.
RM-R14A-F015.explanation: The same sword is called “Kanshou” and later “Kashou.” This is a small name-spelling inconsistency; the other two misspellings concern ordinary words.
RM-R14A-F015.sourceReading: The same sword name 干将 appears as “Kanshou” on page 72 and “Kashou” on page 99. The other two anchors contain ordinary English spelling errors.

RM-S0615-F003.description: The English keeps the casual greeting but drops the joking senior-role address. This is a local address joke rather than evidence for this dossier's character claim.
RM-S0615-F003.explanation: The English keeps the casual greeting but drops the joking senior-role address. This is a local address joke rather than evidence for this dossier's character claim.
RM-S0615-F003.sourceReading: Illya greets Rin with a senior-role address and a slangy form of greeting.

RM-S15A-F019.description: The Japanese attributes the remembered name to another girl. The English instead calls Sella the “other caretaker” and makes Illya the apparent speaker.
RM-S15A-F019.explanation: The Japanese attributes the remembered name to another girl. The English instead calls Sella the “other caretaker” and makes Illya the apparent speaker.
RM-S15A-F019.sourceReading: Shirou remembers Illya’s caretaker as the woman another girl called Sella.

RM-S15I-F013.description: Zouken’s assessment of Sakura to his fellow observer becomes a remark addressed to Sakura as “you.” The prediction itself remains.
RM-S15I-F013.explanation: Zouken’s assessment of Sakura to his fellow observer becomes a remark addressed to Sakura as “you.” The prediction itself remains.
RM-S15I-F013.sourceReading: Watching Sakura with Assassin, Zouken assesses how long she has retained her identity and predicts her transformation. Assassin immediately responds to that assessment.

RM-R2-007.description: The English still targets Rin, naming her immediately after 'you.' The remaining issue is the spelling 'Toshaka,' rather than a change in whom Issei intends to confront.
RM-R2-007.explanation: The English still targets Rin, naming her immediately after 'you.' The remaining issue is the spelling 'Toshaka,' rather than a change in whom Issei intends to confront.
RM-R2-007.sourceReading: Issei declares that he can no longer leave Rin unchecked and then demands that Shirou confide in him.

RM-S1101-F002.description: Illya briefly calls him “big brother” while demanding acknowledgment that he belongs to her. English uses “Shirou,” removing the family address from that coercive question.
RM-S1101-F002.explanation: Illya briefly calls him “big brother” while demanding acknowledgment that he belongs to her. English uses “Shirou,” removing the family address from that coercive question.
RM-S1101-F002.sourceReading: Illya switches from シロウ to repeated お兄ちゃん when asking him to acknowledge that he belongs to her, then returns to シロウ afterward.

RM-S15I-F023.description: The singular Servant just identified as Angra Mainyu becomes plural “Servants.” This changes the referent of the inherited power, rather than anyone’s form of address.
RM-S15I-F023.explanation: The singular Servant just identified as Angra Mainyu becomes plural “Servants.” This changes the referent of the inherited power, rather than anyone’s form of address.
RM-S15I-F023.sourceReading: Rin first names Angra Mainyu and then refers back to that Servant and the power Sakura inherited.

RM-R5A-F005.explanation: Saber's praise keeps Taiga's honesty but drops her resistance to deception. It does not explicitly call her gullible, but it removes one half of the compliment.

RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F001.description: Issei's searching, reformulated warning becomes two blunt statements. His concern survives; the English also contains a local word-order error.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F001.explanation: Issei's searching, reformulated warning becomes two blunt statements. His concern survives; the English also contains a local word-order error.
RM-FATE-D1-ROUTES-F001.sourceReading: Issei searches for a formulation: Shirou goes too far, or perhaps will wear himself down if this continues.

RM-R04F-F003.description: 'Paragon' preserves Shirou's grand introduction but replaces Issei's iron firmness with general excellence.
RM-R04F-F003.explanation: 'Paragon' preserves Shirou's grand introduction but replaces Issei's iron firmness with general excellence.

RM-R5A-F012.description: Issei's specific invocation becomes an unspecified Buddhist sutra. The religious joke and uncertainty about his seriousness remain.

RM-S0613-F001.description: The Japanese has Issei captivated by the woman drawing water. The English gives the water-fetching to Issei and reduces what he admires to her general looks.
RM-S0613-F001.explanation: The Japanese has Issei captivated by the woman drawing water. The English gives the water-fetching to Issei and reduces what he admires to her general looks.

RM-R2-004.description: Rin's teasing question changes clubroom upkeep into classroom upkeep. His diligence remains, but the work she names changes.
RM-R2-004.explanation: Rin's teasing question changes clubroom upkeep into classroom upkeep. His diligence remains, but the work she names changes.
RM-R2-004.sourceReading: Rin asks whether Issei is tending the clubrooms, as part of her recurring tease about his diligence.

RM-R04F-F004.description: Shirou predicts compatibility through Issei's stiff seriousness. The English substitutes intelligence as the reason he might get along with Saber.
RM-R04F-F004.explanation: Shirou predicts compatibility through Issei's stiff seriousness. The English substitutes intelligence as the reason he might get along with Saber.
RM-R04F-F004.sourceReading: Shirou suggests that Issei's stiff seriousness may make him a compatible conversational partner for Saber.

RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F014.description: Issei's concern about what would make him a bad friend becomes an admission that he made Shirou late, even though they arrived in time.
RM-FATE-D1-SCHOOL-F014.explanation: Issei's concern about what would make him a bad friend becomes an admission that he made Shirou late, even though they arrived in time.

RM-S0207-F016.description: Issei's joke about taking charge of temple cooking becomes a joke about joining a circus, breaking the connection between his poor lunch and his proposed remedy.
RM-S0207-F016.explanation: Issei's joke about taking charge of temple cooking becomes a joke about joining a circus, breaking the connection between his poor lunch and his proposed remedy.

RM-S0505-F011.description: Shirou's inability to explain their closeness becomes an explanation cut short by Issei's departure. This changes the local limit on what Shirou can share.

RM-S0505-F011.sourceReading: Shirou could not possibly explain that much about how he and Rin became close; Issei leaves reeling.

RM-S0729-F004.description: The narration changes an unabashed, inconsiderate stare into an intent gaze. Issei's coldness toward strangers remains explicit immediately afterward.
RM-S0729-F004.explanation: The narration changes an unabashed, inconsiderate stare into an intent gaze. Issei's coldness toward strangers remains explicit immediately afterward.
RM-S0729-F004.sourceReading: Issei directs an unrestrained, socially inconsiderate look at the unfamiliar Saber.

RM-S05D-F023.description: Shirou's report that breakfast is mostly prepared becomes a report that cleanup has just finished, changing the work Sakura finds him doing.
RM-S05D-F023.explanation: Shirou's report that breakfast is mostly prepared becomes a report that cleanup has just finished, changing the work Sakura finds him doing.
RM-S05D-F023.sourceReading: Shirou says he has mostly dealt with making breakfast, answering Sakura's question about that task.

RM-S06A-F009.description: A joke about urgent laundry protecting Shirou's household standing becomes a joke about purification and choosing silence. The feared social consequence changes.
RM-S06A-F009.explanation: A joke about urgent laundry protecting Shirou's household standing becomes a joke about purification and choosing silence. The feared social consequence changes.
RM-S06A-F009.sourceReading: Shirou imagines urgently bleaching and spin-drying the evidence to avoid losing his standing to speak in the household.

RM-S0512A-F002.description: Shirou's observation of Rin's assured cooking becomes an inability to see her, removing the evidence behind his decision to leave dinner to her.
RM-S0512A-F002.explanation: Shirou's observation of Rin's assured cooking becomes an inability to see her, removing the evidence behind his decision to leave dinner to her.
RM-S0512A-F002.sourceReading: Watching Rin from behind, Shirou sees no sign of uncertain handling despite the loud cooking noises.

RM-R04D-F005.description: The English gives Saber the action of setting down tea that Shirou serves to her, removing a small act of care beside his protective words.
RM-R04D-F005.explanation: The English gives Saber the action of setting down tea that Shirou serves to her, removing a small act of care beside his protective words.
RM-R04D-F005.sourceReading: Shirou places after-meal tea before Saber after telling her not to risk using her Noble Phantasm.

RM-R04H-F003.description: Dinner remains a welcome for Saber, but its stated role as thanks for the previous night disappears. The meal loses an explicit element of reciprocity.
RM-R04H-F003.explanation: Dinner remains a welcome for Saber, but its stated role as thanks for the previous night disappears. The meal loses an explicit element of reciprocity.

RM-S06F11A-F008.description: The English keeps the broken-VCR joke but changes “I'd sooner fix that” into “this is like fixing that,” softening the heater's exaggerated difficulty.
RM-S06F11A-F008.explanation: The English keeps the broken-VCR joke but changes “I'd sooner fix that” into “this is like fixing that,” softening the heater's exaggerated difficulty.
RM-S06F11A-F008.sourceReading: Shirou had complained that he would sooner repair Taiga's bisected VCR than tackle the heater.

RM-R10F-F010.description: Cod hot pot becomes unspecified cod. Shirou's balanced meal planning survives, while the particular dinner he has planned is less concrete.
RM-R10F-F010.explanation: Cod hot pot becomes unspecified cod. Shirou's balanced meal planning survives, while the particular dinner he has planned is less concrete.

RM-S11E-F002.description: Illya's suggestion that Shirou should have cooked instead becomes a suggestion that he should help mediate while the sisters cook.
RM-S11E-F002.explanation: Illya's suggestion that Shirou should have cooked instead becomes a suggestion that he should help mediate while the sisters cook.
RM-S11E-F002.sourceReading: Illya says Shirou could have cooked himself as the compromise instead of assigning Rin and Sakura together.

RM-R5D-F001.description: Taiga's teasing description of Shirou's fussiness becomes praise of his sharp observation. His noticing Sakura's habit remains intact.
RM-R5D-F001.explanation: Taiga's teasing description of Shirou's fussiness becomes praise of his sharp observation. His noticing Sakura's habit remains intact.

RM-HF-D4-PACT-DINNER-F010.description: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.

RM-R6A-F002.description: A precise instruction to heat the empty pan until it smokes becomes generic preheating. Shirou's practical reassurance to Taiga remains.
RM-R6A-F002.explanation: A precise instruction to heat the empty pan until it smokes becomes generic preheating. Shirou's practical reassurance to Taiga remains.

RM-FATE-D7-ILLYA-PARK-F018.explanation: A snack Shirou planned to share with Saber becomes one bought to give her, replacing planned companionship with a gift.

RM-R7C-002.description: The English generalizes preparation for after school into keeping going. That small timing loss does not support this household dossier.
RM-R7C-002.explanation: The English generalizes preparation for after school into keeping going. That small timing loss does not support this household dossier.

RM-S05C-F020.explanation: Taiga's instruction that Shirou provide fresh sheets becomes her promise to bring them, shifting one part of Sakura's care from him to her.

RM-P1-067.description: Rin's surprise that Archer recognizes her worth more clearly than she does becomes a belief that his praise exceeds her worth.
RM-P1-067.explanation: Rin's surprise that Archer recognizes her worth more clearly than she does becomes a belief that his praise exceeds her worth.
RM-P1-067.sourceReading: Archer recognizes Rin's worth more clearly than she herself does.

RM-S0404B-F006.description: The English preserves Rin's case for an alliance while making Archer's expected partial contribution less explicit.
RM-S0404B-F006.explanation: The English preserves Rin's case for an alliance while making Archer's expected partial contribution less explicit.

RM-R6B-F007.description: Rin calls Archer contrary in Japanese; the English more specifically describes him as disliking people, while retaining her judgment that he is good.

RM-P3-026.explanation: Rin's report that Archer criticized both rescues becomes a prediction about their difficulty. His spoken complaint remains, but its explicit scope is lost.

RM-R7I-001.description: Rin's admission that the Command Spell cannot make up for what happened becomes an admission that her apology is late.

RM-P1-069.description: Rin's acknowledgment that Archer can handle the immediate penalty becomes a taunt about whether he can. Her threat that it will persist into battle remains.

RM-P2-003.description: Rin's rejection of a tea-serving attendant becomes a rejection of being a tea snob, changing the role at issue in their exchange.
RM-P2-003.explanation: Rin's rejection of a tea-serving attendant becomes a rejection of being a tea snob, changing the role at issue in their exchange.

RM-R7I-002.description: Shirou's straightforward wish for consideration becomes awkwardly phrased, though his embarrassment remains understandable.

RM-R7I-009.explanation: Rin's statement that her training was hard becomes a claim that it was harder than Shirou's, anticipating a comparison he makes himself.

RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F006.description: Shirou's goal remains in English, but his insistence that he must not abandon it disappears.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F006.explanation: Shirou's goal remains in English, but his insistence that he must not abandon it disappears.
RM-FATE-D1-EVENING-F006.sourceReading: Becoming a hero remains a goal Shirou must not betray or abandon.

RM-LE-001.description: The English adds an explicit prediction of failed rescue to this recollection. That prediction appears in Archer's supplied day-seven speech, but is absent from this Japanese passage.

RM-FATE-D1-TRAINING-F018.explanation: Shirou's insistence that he must become a hero like Kiritsugu becomes a statement that he wants to.

RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F007.explanation: The survivors Shirou can save become survivors who can save others, changing Archer's criticism of the limits of rescue.

RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F001.description: Shirou's doubt about his own motives as a hero becomes doubt about the value of always doing right.

RM-R14V-F015.description: English makes Archer's condemnation explicitly moral, where the Japanese calls the ideal untenable and explains it as a fairy tale.
RM-R14V-F015.explanation: English makes Archer's condemnation explicitly moral, where the Japanese calls the ideal untenable and explains it as a fairy tale.

RM-R2S-007.description: The English preserves admiration for the ideal but drops the question of whether Archer had once longed to live by it.

RM-S08D-F010.description: English restates Shirou's resolve but omits his reminder that he had already declared this commitment.
RM-S08D-F010.explanation: English restates Shirou's resolve but omits his reminder that he had already declared this commitment.
