RM-R11A-F001.sourceReading: Once his remaining will disappears, nothing remains for him but death.

RM-S06F11A-F013.description: An unresolved search for the meaning of his solitary survival becomes an achieved sense of purpose through helping others. This changes why Shirou says he kept himself constantly occupied.
RM-S06F11A-F013.explanation: An unresolved search for the meaning of his solitary survival becomes an achieved sense of purpose through helping others. This changes why Shirou says he kept himself constantly occupied.
RM-S06F11A-F013.sourceReading: He ran around town searching for meaning in having been the only one saved.

RM-R14AD-F004.description: The reaching gesture still recalls the earlier rescue, but the gray sky disappears. The loss is a specific visual connection, not the entire connection to the fire.
RM-R14AD-F004.explanation: The reaching gesture still recalls the earlier rescue, but the gray sky disappears. The loss is a specific visual connection, not the entire connection to the fire.
RM-R14AD-F004.sourceReading: The raised arm recreates the remembered scene beneath that day's gray sky.

RM-S09E-F011.description: Saving others remains his purpose, but the English shifts from what has allowed him to keep living to how he has chosen to live. This softens the personal dependence expressed at this decision.
RM-S09E-F011.explanation: Saving others remains his purpose, but the English shifts from what has allowed him to keep living to how he has chosen to live. This softens the personal dependence expressed at this decision.
RM-S09E-F011.sourceReading: The commitment to save people from arbitrary calamity has enabled or justified his continuing to live.

RM-S13B-F017.description: The Japanese names the victims' voices as something he could betray. The English asks only about betraying himself, although the following page still states his obligation to the dead.
RM-S13B-F017.explanation: The Japanese names the victims' voices as something he could betray. The English asks only about betraying himself, although the following page still states his obligation to the dead.
RM-S13B-F017.sourceReading: He asks whether he will betray both the dying people's voices and his former self struggling to survive alone.

RM-S0914-F002.description: The English reverses the envy. Shirou envies his rescuer's extraordinary happiness; the translation makes the rescuer appear envious of Shirou.
RM-S0914-F002.explanation: The English reverses the envy. Shirou envies his rescuer's extraordinary happiness; the translation makes the rescuer appear envious of Shirou.
RM-S0914-F002.sourceReading: Kiritsugu's grateful happiness is so striking that even the dying Shirou can envy him.

RM-S1009B-F004.description: The Japanese connects his calm to seeing others die as he is now dying. The English instead emphasizes that they are already dead. This changes the expressed reason without proving indifference to them.
RM-S1009B-F004.explanation: The Japanese connects his calm to seeing others die as he is now dying. The English instead emphasizes that they are already dead. This changes the expressed reason without proving indifference to them.
RM-S1009B-F004.sourceReading: He is unafraid because he recognizes that he cannot survive and that the people around him died in the same manner.

RM-S1517B-F031.description: The source explains where Shirou saw the mourners. The English instead says the death toll required mass funerals, adding a logistical explanation the passage does not give.
RM-S1517B-F031.explanation: The source explains where Shirou saw the mourners. The English instead says the death toll required mass funerals, adding a logistical explanation the passage does not give.
RM-S1517B-F031.sourceReading: He saw grieving people as well as dying people; funerals held in a large building explain his encounter with the mourners.

RM-S0400B-F005.description: The rescue still involves a burned, dying child, but his explicit unconsciousness is omitted. No further conclusion about his awareness or memory follows.
RM-S0400B-F005.explanation: The rescue still involves a burned, dying child, but his explicit unconsciousness is omitted. No further conclusion about his awareness or memory follows.
RM-S0400B-F005.sourceReading: Kiritsugu carries out a child who is unconscious, burned all over, and near death, rejoicing with tears in his eyes.

RM-S0914-F004.description: Shirou's reluctance to recognize his own hope becomes a dream of not noticing something. The next page preserves his wish for relief, but its concealed place in his motives is obscured.
RM-S0914-F004.explanation: Shirou's reluctance to recognize his own hope becomes a dream of not noticing something. The next page preserves his wish for relief, but its concealed place in his motives is obscured.
RM-S0914-F004.sourceReading: Somewhere within himself, he harbored a dream while avoiding awareness of it: smiling like Kiritsugu might bring him relief too.

RM-S1517B-F032.description: An emptied inner life governed by “I must go on to be forgiven” becomes movement “void of all reason.” The English loses the specific obligation driving him.
RM-S1517B-F032.explanation: An emptied inner life governed by “I must go on to be forgiven” becomes movement “void of all reason.” The English loses the specific obligation driving him.
RM-S1517B-F032.sourceReading: With his inner self emptied out, he believed he would not be forgiven unless he nevertheless kept moving forward.

RM-S1517B-F038.description: Sorrow and radiant memories coexist in the Japanese. The English instead says suffering makes goodness brighter, changing the reasoning behind Shirou's defense of remembrance.
RM-S1517B-F038.explanation: Sorrow and radiant memories coexist in the Japanese. The English instead says suffering makes goodness brighter, changing the reasoning behind Shirou's defense of remembrance.
RM-S1517B-F038.sourceReading: Death is sorrowful and also leaves radiant memories; pain is not its only legacy.

RM-S0400B-F004.description: Shirou's quiet vigil over his father becomes another description of Kiritsugu looking at the moon and dying. The child's act of watching is lost.
RM-S0400B-F004.explanation: Shirou's quiet vigil over his father becomes another description of Kiritsugu looking at the moon and dying. The child's act of watching is lost.
RM-S0400B-F004.sourceReading: After Kiritsugu dies, Shirou does nothing but look up at the winter moon and his deceased father.

RM-S1517B-F039.description: The deaths still influence Shirou, but being bound by them becomes being shaped by them. This weakens the contrast between their constraint and Kiritsugu's protective memory.
RM-S1517B-F039.explanation: The deaths still influence Shirou, but being bound by them becomes being shaped by them. This weakens the contrast between their constraint and Kiritsugu's protective memory.
RM-S1517B-F039.sourceReading: The deaths continue to bind him, while memories of Kiritsugu protect him.

RM-S06A-F001.description: The father's assurance that Shirou can go alone becomes the mother's order that the father must not go alone. Speaker, addressee, and instruction all change.
RM-S06A-F001.explanation: The father's assurance that Shirou can go alone becomes the mother's order that the father must not go alone. Speaker, addressee, and instruction all change.
RM-S06A-F001.sourceReading: His father asks or affirms that the child can go alone, then tells him to wait outside.

RM-S13A-F016.description: What sustained Shirou becomes something he rejects, instead of something that now rejects him. The change alters the direction of his internal accusation.
RM-S13A-F016.explanation: What sustained Shirou becomes something he rejects, instead of something that now rejects him. The change alters the direction of his internal accusation.
RM-S13A-F016.sourceReading: What has sustained him would turn against and negate him if he allowed the tragedy to recur.

RM-R11B-F005.description: A sediment-like feeling becomes a falling cage. His enjoyment and self-denial remain, but the image expressing their collision changes.
RM-R11B-F005.explanation: A sediment-like feeling becomes a falling cage. His enjoyment and self-denial remain, but the image expressing their collision changes.
RM-R11B-F005.sourceReading: Something like sediment or dregs descends as he recognizes his enjoyment and tells himself he does not deserve it.

RM-R04B-F006.description: The sentence replaces explicit awareness of Saber as a woman with thinking she is real. This repeats the same attraction-related change in another route.
RM-R04B-F006.explanation: The sentence replaces explicit awareness of Saber as a woman with thinking she is real. This repeats the same attraction-related change in another route.
RM-R04B-F006.sourceReading: Shirou becomes conscious of Saber as a woman because her ordinary clothes make her presence feel immediate and familiar.

RM-S0508X-F019.description: Saber's apparent advantage in basic combat becomes Archer's advantage. Her caution about his unrevealed techniques and weapon remains.
RM-S0508X-F019.explanation: Saber's apparent advantage in basic combat becomes Archer's advantage. Her caution about his unrevealed techniques and weapon remains.
RM-S0508X-F019.sourceReading: Saber believes she exceeds Archer in basic combat ability, while withholding judgment on his techniques and Noble Phantasm.

RM-S1513B-F012.description: The English simplifies an inverted, arm-powered leap into catching a fall and springing upward. This reduces choreography detail without removing Saber's successful resistance.
RM-S1513B-F012.explanation: The English simplifies an inverted, arm-powered leap into catching a fall and springing upward. This reduces choreography detail without removing Saber's successful resistance.
RM-S1513B-F012.sourceReading: Saber reverses her body while inverted and leaps a substantial distance using only her arms.

RM-S16A-F020.description: Saber's involuntary staggering becomes a planted stance. The resulting opening for Rider remains, but its physical cause changes.
RM-S16A-F020.explanation: Saber's involuntary staggering becomes a planted stance. The resulting opening for Rider remains, but its physical cause changes.
RM-S16A-F020.sourceReading: Saber staggers after deflecting the sword and cannot pursue Rider, creating the two-second opening.

RM-HF-D10A-F007.description: Shirou's stated atonement for Saber's death becomes repayment for her cooperation. 'Also' becomes 'the only way,' changing both the expressed cost of following him and his reason for continuing.
RM-HF-D10A-F007.explanation: Shirou's stated atonement for Saber's death becomes repayment for her cooperation. 'Also' becomes 'the only way,' changing both the expressed cost of following him and his reason for continuing.
RM-HF-D10A-F007.sourceReading: Continuing the fight is also atonement toward Saber, whom Shirou understands to have died after going along with his selfishness.

RM-HF-D10E-F011.description: The English adds disembowelment to the apparent corpse while retaining uncertainty through 'looks like.' This supports a separate finding about added gore, not a claim about Saber's motives.
RM-HF-D10E-F011.explanation: The English adds disembowelment to the apparent corpse while retaining uncertainty through 'looks like.' This supports a separate finding about added gore, not a claim about Saber's motives.
RM-HF-D10E-F011.sourceReading: Something resembling Berserker's corpse is sinking into the Shadow.

RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F012.description: The sentence needs 'the world,' but it still conveys Saber's confidence that Rin would not cause worldwide chaos.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F012.explanation: The sentence needs 'the world,' but it still conveys Saber's confidence that Rin would not cause worldwide chaos.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F012.sourceReading: Saber believes Rin's self-interested wish would not plunge the world into chaos.

RM-S1200B-F009.description: The English changes the relation between leaving the war and receiving help. The Japanese links ceasing to be a Master with becoming able to repent; the English makes the former a concession while retaining remorse as a condition.
RM-S1200B-F009.explanation: The English changes the relation between leaving the war and receiving help. The Japanese links ceasing to be a Master with becoming able to repent; the English makes the former a concession while retaining remorse as a condition.
RM-S1200B-F009.sourceReading: Shirou envisages Illya ceasing to be a Master and becoming capable of regretting her actions as the premise for helping her.

RM-HF-D10C-F006.description: Shirou's objection to either girl being injured becomes a warning that Rin will be hurt. His explicit concern for Illya within this appeal disappears.
RM-HF-D10C-F006.explanation: Shirou's objection to either girl being injured becomes a warning that Rin will be hurt. His explicit concern for Illya within this appeal disappears.
RM-HF-D10C-F006.sourceReading: Shirou objects because either Rin or Illya will be injured if they fight.

RM-HF-D10C-F019.description: The English adds an order from Illya where the Japanese simply says Berserker stops. It makes her direct the halt, although the source leaves its immediate cause unstated.
RM-HF-D10C-F019.explanation: The English adds an order from Illya where the Japanese simply says Berserker stops. It makes her direct the halt, although the source leaves its immediate cause unstated.
RM-HF-D10C-F019.sourceReading: Illya vaguely realizes escape from her fear is impossible, and the narration then states that Berserker stops.

RM-HF-D10E-F012.description: The explanation of Illya's fear loses the immediate threat to her own life. It describes her witnessing Berserker's death instead of facing both his defeat and approaching death herself.
RM-HF-D10E-F012.explanation: The explanation of Illya's fear loses the immediate threat to her own life. It describes her witnessing Berserker's death instead of facing both his defeat and approaching death herself.
RM-HF-D10E-F012.sourceReading: Illya faces both her Servant's defeat and death immediately threatening her.

RM-S0305-F015.description: The English keeps Illya's casual threat but loses the image of crushing the Servants and her treatment of them as animals. Her murderous intent remains clear.
RM-S0305-F015.explanation: The English keeps Illya's casual threat but loses the image of crushing the Servants and her treatment of them as animals. Her murderous intent remains clear.
RM-S0305-F015.sourceReading: Illya speaks of crushing both Servants together and counts them with the animal classifier 匹.

RM-HF-D10G-F012.description: The English supplies a lobby as Illya's destination. It preserves the dismissal and her refusal to leave Shirou alone, so this detail does not support the character dossier.
RM-HF-D10G-F012.explanation: The English supplies a lobby as Illya's destination. It preserves the dismissal and her refusal to leave Shirou alone, so this detail does not support the character dossier.
RM-HF-D10G-F012.sourceReading: Kotomine tells Illya to leave the room if she has no business there.

RM-S0307-F002.description: The English replaces a one-strike requirement with urgency. This changes the tactical instruction without removing Illya's intent to kill Saber.
RM-S0307-F002.explanation: The English replaces a one-strike requirement with urgency. This changes the tactical instruction without removing Illya's intent to kill Saber.
RM-S0307-F002.sourceReading: Illya orders a single killing strike because Saber regenerates.

RM-HF-D10H-F019.description: Illya's offer to treat Sakura as human becomes unspecified special treatment. The English retains condescension but removes the precise insult that Sakura turns back on her.
RM-HF-D10H-F019.explanation: Illya's offer to treat Sakura as human becomes unspecified special treatment. The English retains condescension but removes the precise insult that Sakura turns back on her.
RM-HF-D10H-F019.sourceReading: Illya grants Sakura the supposed exception of being treated as human because she knows Shirou.

RM-HF-D10I-F004.description: Illya's judgment that Archer goes unrewarded becomes general sympathy for him. Her rejection of jealousy remains, but the reason she gives for her concern is less specific.
RM-HF-D10I-F004.explanation: Illya's judgment that Archer goes unrewarded becomes general sympathy for him. Her rejection of jealousy remains, but the reason she gives for her concern is less specific.
RM-HF-D10I-F004.sourceReading: Illya says Archer has gone unrewarded or has not received a fitting return, rejecting Taiga's suggestion of jealousy.

RM-HF-D10F-F002.description: The sentence “I don’t what you’re talking about” lacks the verb “know.” Illya’s denial remains understandable.
RM-HF-D10F-F002.explanation: The sentence “I don’t what you’re talking about” lacks the verb “know.” Illya’s denial remains understandable.
RM-HF-D10F-F002.sourceReading: Illya denies knowing what Rin means and denies having been happy about the stay.

RM-R5B-F015.description: Rider's voice changes from chillingly beautiful to surprisingly beautiful and sensual. Attraction remains, but its expressly unsettling quality is weakened.
RM-R5B-F015.explanation: Rider's voice changes from chillingly beautiful to surprisingly beautiful and sensual. Attraction remains, but its expressly unsettling quality is weakened.
RM-R5B-F015.sourceReading: Rider's irritated voice is simultaneously beautiful enough to send a shiver through Shirou.

RM-S0600-F007.description: The English keeps Shirou's retreat but drops his difficulty getting the question out. Rider's intimidating presence remains evident in the surrounding description.
RM-S0600-F007.explanation: The English keeps Shirou's retreat but drops his difficulty getting the question out. Rider's intimidating presence remains evident in the surrounding description.
RM-S0600-F007.sourceReading: After experiencing an intense chill, Shirou retreats slightly and manages to get his question out.

RM-R5C-F002.description: Both rescue branches change the intercepted target from Rider's nail to Rider herself. The rescue remains, but the English adds a bodily hit that these sentences do not describe.
RM-R5C-F002.explanation: Both rescue branches change the intercepted target from Rider's nail to Rider herself. The rescue remains, but the English adds a bodily hit that these sentences do not describe.
RM-R5C-F002.sourceReading: In both branches, the nail remains the subject across the interrupted sentence and is knocked aside by the incoming light projectiles.

RM-S0601B-F006.description: Rider's observation that Shinji wants to win Shirou over becomes an explanation of why Shinji likes him. 'Noble soul' also heightens the praise, though the Japanese genuinely acknowledges Shirou's kindness.
RM-S0601B-F006.explanation: Rider's observation that Shinji wants to win Shirou over becomes an explanation of why Shinji likes him. 'Noble soul' also heightens the praise, though the Japanese genuinely acknowledges Shirou's kindness.
RM-S0601B-F006.sourceReading: Rider comments on Shirou's good nature and understands why Shinji would try to win him over.

RM-R7E-009.description: The English specifies her spine where the Japanese says her neck. The surrounding lines still locate the fatal injury at the neck; this does not establish a change to Rider's characterization.
RM-R7E-009.explanation: The English specifies her spine where the Japanese says her neck. The surrounding lines still locate the fatal injury at the neck; this does not establish a change to Rider's characterization.
RM-R7E-009.sourceReading: Shirou describes severing Rider's neck in one blow, then questions whether severing accurately describes the wound.

RM-HF-D14C-F007.description: The English states that Sakura is no longer holding back where the Japanese presents that as an explanation the narrator is considering. Both versions call Rider's action a betrayal.
RM-HF-D14C-F007.explanation: The English states that Sakura is no longer holding back where the Japanese presents that as an explanation the narrator is considering. Both versions call Rider's action a betrayal.
RM-HF-D14C-F007.sourceReading: The shadow covers the courtyard; the narrator conjectures that Rider's betrayal may have made Sakura become serious.

RM-S0908-F006.description: The English leaves the kick's roundhouse form unspecified while preserving its target and force.
RM-S0908-F006.explanation: The English leaves the kick's roundhouse form unspecified while preserving its target and force.
RM-S0908-F006.sourceReading: A single roundhouse kick to Shirou's abdomen sends him through the window.

RM-HF-D4-PARK-F005.description: Shinji's excuse that killing Saber would be unavoidable becomes praise of Rider as unstoppable. Rider still obeys his order in the next sentence.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F005.explanation: Shinji's excuse that killing Saber would be unavoidable becomes praise of Rider as unstoppable. Rider still obeys his order in the next sentence.
RM-HF-D4-PARK-F005.sourceReading: Shinji claims compliance with his grandfather's instructions and excuses killing Shirou's Servant as something unavoidable.

RM-S0912-F013.description: Rider's assurance that nobody can stop her advance becomes a comparison of agility. Her concession to Saber and confidence in her Noble Phantasm remain.
RM-S0912-F013.explanation: Rider's assurance that nobody can stop her advance becomes a comparison of agility. Her concession to Saber and confidence in her Noble Phantasm remain.
RM-S0912-F013.sourceReading: After conceding her inferiority to Saber, Rider says no opponent can obstruct her rapid advance.

RM-S1003B-F011.description: The witness reads 'bought' where 'brought' is evidently intended. Rider's reason for choosing the location remains clear.
RM-S1003B-F011.explanation: The witness reads 'bought' where 'brought' is evidently intended. Rider's reason for choosing the location remains clear.
RM-S1003B-F011.sourceReading: Rider explains that she lured Saber to a location where she could use her Noble Phantasm without other Masters observing.

RM-S08C-F043.description: Rider's earnest request to repeat the thanks becomes Shirou's thought that she will hear him. The change removes his observation of how seriously she receives the unexpected gratitude.
RM-S08C-F043.explanation: Rider's earnest request to repeat the thanks becomes Shirou's thought that she will hear him. The change removes his observation of how seriously she receives the unexpected gratitude.
RM-S08C-F043.sourceReading: Shirou remarks that Rider is earnestly asking what he just said, adding to his embarrassment about thanking her.

RM-TD05-F009.description: The English reduces an abdominal rupture and immediate death to general lethality. This belongs with the treatment of bodily injury and Shirou's survival.
RM-TD05-F009.explanation: The English reduces an abdominal rupture and immediate death to general lethality. This belongs with the treatment of bodily injury and Shirou's survival.
RM-TD05-F009.sourceReading: Illya says that ordinarily the roundhouse would rupture Shirou's abdomen and kill him immediately.

RM-S09A-F015.description: Rider's acknowledgment that she underestimated Shirou becomes an admission that she lost focus. This removes her recognition of his successful concentration.
RM-S09A-F015.explanation: Rider's acknowledgment that she underestimated Shirou becomes an admission that she lost focus. This removes her recognition of his successful concentration.
RM-S09A-F015.sourceReading: Rider apologizes for underestimating Shirou's concentration after he predicts her attacks and briefly passes her.

RM-S09D-F005.description: Rider's grip on Shinji's arm becomes Shinji clinging to hers. Her verbal refusal to let him hurt Sakura remains, but the physical expression of that refusal changes.
RM-S09D-F005.explanation: Rider's grip on Shinji's arm becomes Shinji clinging to hers. Her verbal refusal to let him hurt Sakura remains, but the physical expression of that refusal changes.
RM-S09D-F005.sourceReading: After Rider releases him, Shinji holds his own arm where she had seized it and staggers backward.

RM-S09G-F019.description: Rider's attacks on the exposed chest and stomach become attacks on the arms and stomach. The English retains the reduced force, but changes the bodily pattern Shirou is assessing.
RM-S09G-F019.explanation: Rider's attacks on the exposed chest and stomach become attacks on the arms and stomach. The English retains the reduced force, but changes the bodily pattern Shirou is assessing.
RM-S09G-F019.sourceReading: Rider strikes only Shirou's exposed abdomen and chest, avoiding the gaps in the arms guarding his head.

RM-S13F-F015.description: The condition for treating Shirou as an enemy changes from Sakura seeing him as one to Rider judging him dangerous. This alters the specific danger Sakura fears from Rider's continuing protection.
RM-S13F-F015.explanation: The condition for treating Shirou as an enemy changes from Sakura seeing him as one to Rider judging him dangerous. This alters the specific danger Sakura fears from Rider's continuing protection.
RM-S13F-F015.sourceReading: Even if Shirou supports Sakura, Sakura's own recognition of him as an enemy would make him an external enemy to be defeated.

RM-HF-D10D-F001.description: The kick's location becomes less precise, while Archer's protective intervention remains clear.
RM-HF-D10D-F001.explanation: The kick's location becomes less precise, while Archer's protective intervention remains clear.
RM-HF-D10D-F001.sourceReading: Assassin is knocked away by a kick to his flank.

RM-R14AB-F001.description: “Freely reels” makes Assassin's effortless handling of the long sword harder to understand. Saber still cannot approach him, so the passage retains his tactical control.
RM-R14AB-F001.explanation: “Freely reels” makes Assassin's effortless handling of the long sword harder to understand. Saber still cannot approach him, so the passage retains his tactical control.
RM-R14AB-F001.sourceReading: Assassin handles the nearly two-meter weapon freely and expertly, preventing Saber from entering her effective range.

RM-S0608B-F009.description: Kojirou's reputation as an exceptional swordsman's worthy rival becomes a claim that he was hailed as the world's greatest swordsman. This removes the relationship that defines his place in the story told about him.
RM-S0608B-F009.explanation: Kojirou's reputation as an exceptional swordsman's worthy rival becomes a claim that he was hailed as the world's greatest swordsman. This removes the relationship that defines his place in the story told about him.
RM-S0608B-F009.sourceReading: Popular tradition elevated the uncertain swordsman as a worthy rival to an exceptional master swordsman.

RM-R14AC-F001.description: The one stance used by a swordsman who normally has none becomes an “imaginary stance.” The change removes what makes this preparation exceptional before Swallow Reversal.
RM-R14AC-F001.explanation: The one stance used by a swordsman who normally has none becomes an “imaginary stance.” The change removes what makes this preparation exceptional before Swallow Reversal.
RM-R14AC-F001.sourceReading: This is Assassin's sole stance, exceptional because he ordinarily has nothing resembling a fixed stance.

RM-S0614-F002.description: The opening comparison changes straight and curved attack paths into straight and curved blades. Later sentences restore the movement contrast, but its introduction gives the wrong explanation.
RM-S0614-F002.explanation: The opening comparison changes straight and curved attack paths into straight and curved blades. Later sentences restore the movement contrast, but its introduction gives the wrong explanation.
RM-S0614-F002.sourceReading: Saber's strokes follow straight paths, whereas Assassin's follow curves; his technique somehow compensates for the longer route.

RM-S15I-F017.description: The English assigns leaving a name and becoming the original to Illya, although Zouken is explaining the skull-masked Assassin's wish. This belongs in a dossier about that character's identity.
RM-S15I-F017.explanation: The English assigns leaving a name and becoming the original to Illya, although Zouken is explaining the skull-masked Assassin's wish. This belongs in a dossier about that character's identity.
RM-S15I-F017.sourceReading: Zouken explains the skull-masked Assassin's wish to leave his own name in history and become an original, enduring as a record.

RM-S16A-F006.description: Sakura's denial of becoming the one authentic Hassan becomes a denial of being a true Hassan. The loss concerns the skull-masked assassin's desired identity.
RM-S16A-F006.explanation: Sakura's denial of becoming the one authentic Hassan becomes a denial of being a true Hassan. The loss concerns the skull-masked assassin's desired identity.
RM-S16A-F006.sourceReading: Sakura denies that the skull-masked assassin can become the sole authentic Hassan, following her rejection of his wish to recover his name.

RM-HF-D10D-F002.description: Assassin's defeated attack becomes a parry performed by Assassin. The exchange is reversed, although Archer's overall advantage remains clear; it concerns the skull-masked Assassin.
RM-HF-D10D-F002.explanation: Assassin's defeated attack becomes a parry performed by Assassin. The exchange is reversed, although Archer's overall advantage remains clear; it concerns the skull-masked Assassin.
RM-HF-D10D-F002.sourceReading: Assassin cries out while retreating after Archer cuts down his all-out attack.

RM-R14AB-F002.description: A one-meter difference in fighting range becomes a one-meter distance between the fighters. This obscures the reach advantage that Saber must overcome.
RM-R14AB-F002.explanation: A one-meter difference in fighting range becomes a one-meter distance between the fighters. This obscures the reach advantage that Saber must overcome.
RM-R14AB-F002.sourceReading: Their effective fighting ranges differ by one meter, a gap Saber cannot close while Assassin controls her approach.

RM-R14AC-F011.description: “In that front” should be “on that front.” The joke about needing training in both swordsmanship and judging women remains understandable.
RM-R14AC-F011.explanation: “In that front” should be “on that front.” The joke about needing training in both swordsmanship and judging women remains understandable.
RM-R14AC-F011.sourceReading: Assassin ruefully jokes that both his swordsmanship and his judgment of women need further training.

RM-P3-012.description: The explanation of spear sweeps becomes a statement that Archer exploits spear tactics. This concerns Lancer's weapon mechanics, not Assassin's swordcraft.
RM-P3-012.explanation: The explanation of spear sweeps becomes a statement that Archer exploits spear tactics. This concerns Lancer's weapon mechanics, not Assassin's swordcraft.
RM-P3-012.sourceReading: The narration explains that sweeping, rather than thrusting, is the spear's basic tactic because its broad reach prevents simple retreat.

RM-HF-D10C-F023.description: Their shared pursuit becomes a claim that they were fated to meet. The individual wishes survive, and this change belongs to Zouken's relationship with the skull-masked Assassin.
RM-HF-D10C-F023.explanation: Their shared pursuit becomes a claim that they were fated to meet. The individual wishes survive, and this change belongs to Zouken's relationship with the skull-masked Assassin.
RM-HF-D10C-F023.sourceReading: Zouken says their related aims explain their current joint pursuit: bodily immortality for him and an enduring name for Assassin.

RM-P3-013.description: A rib-crushing blow from the spear's shaft becomes impalement. This is a separate error in Lancer's combat explanation.
RM-P3-013.explanation: A rib-crushing blow from the spear's shaft becomes impalement. This is a separate error in Lancer's combat explanation.
RM-P3-013.sourceReading: A reckless advance exposes Archer to a blow from the spear's long shaft that can crush his ribs.

RM-S0614-F003.description: Calling his sword “wicked” loses the explicit description of his technique as unorthodox. It can still refer figuratively to his swordsmanship, so it does not establish an evil artifact or a morally evil swordsman.
RM-S0614-F003.explanation: Calling his sword “wicked” loses the explicit description of his technique as unorthodox. It can still refer figuratively to his swordsmanship, so it does not establish an evil artifact or a morally evil swordsman.
RM-S0614-F003.sourceReading: Assassin calls his swordsmanship unorthodox, then links his unusual skills to being an exponent of that style.

RM-S0302-F034.description: A towering religious symbol becomes reverence in Kotomine's voice and devotion in his eyes. This adds an appearance of piety that the Japanese leaves unstated.
RM-S0302-F034.explanation: A towering religious symbol becomes reverence in Kotomine's voice and devotion in his eyes. This adds an appearance of piety that the Japanese leaves unstated.
RM-S0302-F034.sourceReading: After Kotomine turns away, a symbol worthy of worship towers in the direction of his gaze.

RM-R3C-F005.description: Rin's remark about Kotomine's skill at cornering people becomes praise for elementary instruction. His subsequent pressure remains, but her pointed recognition of it disappears.
RM-R3C-F005.explanation: Rin's remark about Kotomine's skill at cornering people becomes praise for elementary instruction. His subsequent pressure remains, but her pointed recognition of it disappears.
RM-R3C-F005.sourceReading: Rin identifies putting someone under pressure or cornering them as Kotomine's specialty.

RM-S1207B-F031.description: 'Student and disciple' removes the teacher from the relationship that explains why Shirou expects Rin to seek Kotomine's protection.
RM-S1207B-F031.explanation: 'Student and disciple' removes the teacher from the relationship that explains why Shirou expects Rin to seek Kotomine's protection.
RM-S1207B-F031.sourceReading: Their teacher-pupil relationship makes seeking Kotomine's protection seem natural to Shirou.

RM-HF-D10H-F003.description: The English adds amusement at Gilgamesh's own wording. The Japanese keeps his mockery directed at Kirei's claim to have no desires.
RM-HF-D10H-F003.explanation: The English adds amusement at Gilgamesh's own wording. The Japanese keeps his mockery directed at Kirei's claim to have no desires.
RM-HF-D10H-F003.sourceReading: The final fragment specifies the priest's words that Gilgamesh appears to mock: his profession of having no desires.

RM-HF-D14B-F034.description: Kiritsugu's suffering displeases Kotomine in the Japanese. The English instead says it makes Kiritsugu unhappy, removing one specific source of Kotomine's resentment.
RM-HF-D14B-F034.explanation: Kiritsugu's suffering displeases Kotomine in the Japanese. The English instead says it makes Kiritsugu unhappy, removing one specific source of Kotomine's resentment.
RM-HF-D14B-F034.sourceReading: Kotomine finds both Kiritsugu's existence and his anguish offensive, continuing his comparison between what Kiritsugu could abandon and what he himself never possessed.

RM-S1504B-F037.description: Kotomine's claim that he cursed Kiritsugu becomes a statement that Kiritsugu cursed himself. This weakens the direct basis for Shirou's ensuing accusation; it does not establish whether Kotomine's account is true.
RM-S1504B-F037.explanation: Kotomine's claim that he cursed Kiritsugu becomes a statement that Kiritsugu cursed himself. This weakens the direct basis for Shirou's ensuing accusation; it does not establish whether Kotomine's account is true.
RM-S1504B-F037.sourceReading: Kotomine says Kiritsugu spared him despite his having cursed Kiritsugu. Shirou then infers responsibility: '切嗣が死んだのはコイツのせいで。' corresponds to 'Kiritsugu died because of Kotomine?'

RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F012.description: Shirou's imagined example of an unacceptable tactic becomes a prediction reported from Kotomine. Saber's reply still rejects the tactic, making the English transition less direct.
RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F012.explanation: Shirou's imagined example of an unacceptable tactic becomes a prediction reported from Kotomine. Saber's reply still rejects the tactic, making the English transition less direct.
RM-HF-D4-SABER-BRIEFING-F012.sourceReading: Recalling the priest's explanation, Shirou imagines involving uninvolved non-Masters and causing a disaster as examples of the means he fears Saber might use.

RM-S07D-F002.description: Shirou's wariness of Kotomine becomes confidence in Kotomine's carefulness. The English substitutes a judgment of competence for the source's warning about dealing with him.
RM-S07D-F002.explanation: Shirou's wariness of Kotomine becomes confidence in Kotomine's carefulness. The English substitutes a judgment of competence for the source's warning about dealing with him.
RM-S07D-F002.sourceReading: Kotomine was someone around whom Shirou could not safely lower his guard.

RM-S08D-F027.description: Gilgamesh's announcement that he will act freely becomes permission for Kirei to do so.
RM-S08D-F027.explanation: Gilgamesh's announcement that he will act freely becomes permission for Kirei to do so.
RM-S08D-F027.sourceReading: After accepting Kirei's inaction, Gilgamesh announces that he will act as he pleases and disappears.

RM-S09F-F025.description: Kotomine's prediction that Rin will kill Sakura becomes a prediction of an attack. The urgency remains, but the stated outcome is less definite.
RM-S09F-F025.explanation: Kotomine's prediction that Rin will kill Sakura becomes a prediction of an attack. The urgency remains, but the stated outcome is less definite.
RM-S09F-F025.sourceReading: Kotomine predicts that Rin will kill Sakura if she finds her first.

RM-R14U-F004.description: Kotomine's regret at losing a capable apprentice becomes an absence of criticism toward a less capable one. The change obscures how his appraisal of Rin accompanies the threat to her life.
RM-R14U-F004.explanation: Kotomine's regret at losing a capable apprentice becomes an absence of criticism toward a less capable one. The change obscures how his appraisal of Rin accompanies the threat to her life.
RM-R14U-F004.sourceReading: A less capable apprentice would give Kotomine no cause for regret at losing her; the deathbed image and Rin's recognition of her fate specify the stakes.

RM-S09H-F013.description: A warning that even the original practitioner could not undo the implantation becomes a claim about Kotomine's training and personal limits. This changes the scope and basis of his medical explanation.
RM-S09H-F013.explanation: A warning that even the original practitioner could not undo the implantation becomes a claim about Kotomine's training and personal limits. This changes the scope and basis of his medical explanation.
RM-S09H-F013.sourceReading: Even the practitioner who implanted the Crest could presumably no longer undo it now that the worms are part of Sakura.

RM-R14U-F005.description: Rin remains Kotomine's apprentice beneath a saintly smile, but she is no longer explicitly called a sacrificial victim. The surrounding threat survives while this religious contrast is reduced.
RM-R14U-F005.explanation: Rin remains Kotomine's apprentice beneath a saintly smile, but she is no longer explicitly called a sacrificial victim. The surrounding threat survives while this religious contrast is reduced.
RM-R14U-F005.sourceReading: Kotomine's saintly smile is directed at a sacrificial victim who was his apprentice for ten years.

RM-S15B-F005.description: The explicit requirement to copy Kotomine exactly is reduced, though the next sentence preserves the danger of a slight mistake. This does not support the proposed character dossier.
RM-S15B-F005.explanation: The explicit requirement to copy Kotomine exactly is reduced, though the next sentence preserves the danger of a slight mistake. This does not support the proposed character dossier.
RM-S15B-F005.sourceReading: Lacking climbing experience, Shirou must copy Kotomine without deviation.

RM-R14U-F006.description: Kotomine says his mentor was easy to betray because of their relationship. The English instead emphasizes his effort in betraying him, losing the taunt about exploiting that bond.
RM-R14U-F006.explanation: Kotomine says his mentor was easy to betray because of their relationship. The English instead emphasizes his effort in betraying him, losing the taunt about exploiting that bond.
RM-R14U-F006.sourceReading: Kotomine says the teacher relationship made his treacherous attack easy.

RM-S05D-F031.description: Saber's possible reasons for attacking become possible reasons for Caster's silence, introducing the suggestion that Caster has been caught red-handed.
RM-S05D-F031.explanation: Saber's possible reasons for attacking become possible reasons for Caster's silence, introducing the suggestion that Caster has been caught red-handed.
RM-S05D-F031.sourceReading: The narrator wonders whether Saber takes Caster's failure to react as an opportunity or an insult, immediately before describing Saber's advance.

RM-S1301B-F004.description: Rin's allowance that Caster underestimated Saber becomes a statement that Caster already knows Saber's superiority. Her suspicion of an unprepared attack remains.
RM-S1301B-F004.explanation: Rin's allowance that Caster underestimated Saber becomes a statement that Caster already knows Saber's superiority. Her suspicion of an unprepared attack remains.
RM-S1301B-F004.sourceReading: Rin allows that Saber may have exceeded Caster's expectations, while questioning whether Caster would attack without precautions.

RM-S1303B-F014.description: Saber dismisses Caster's tragic experience in Japanese; English has her dismiss Caster's misdeeds, changing Caster's role in the reply from sufferer to wrongdoer.
RM-S1303B-F014.explanation: Saber dismisses Caster's tragic experience in Japanese; English has her dismiss Caster's misdeeds, changing Caster's role in the reply from sufferer to wrongdoer.
RM-S1303B-F014.sourceReading: Saber dismisses Caster's unhappy or unjust fate, responding to her complaint about having been used by others.

RM-R9A-F016.description: Archer's concession that Caster is morally unscrupulous becomes a concession that she schemes. Rin's condemnation remains, but his agreement with its ethical substance is less explicit.
RM-R9A-F016.explanation: Archer's concession that Caster is morally unscrupulous becomes a concession that she schemes. Rin's condemnation remains, but his agreement with its ethical substance is less explicit.
RM-R9A-F016.sourceReading: Archer concedes Caster's moral unscrupulousness before praising her conduct as characteristic of a mage.

RM-R7F-005.description: Archer's prediction that Caster would remove her Master's authority at the outset becomes an abstract rejection of having a Master. Her manipulation of that person remains explicit.
RM-R7F-005.explanation: Archer's prediction that Caster would remove her Master's authority at the outset becomes an abstract rejection of having a Master. Her manipulation of that person remains explicit.
RM-R7F-005.sourceReading: Archer theorizes that Caster would immediately remove the Master as an obstacle or authority and use them for her convenience. His account is subsequently reconsidered in favor of deception.

RM-TD78-S1300-F026.description: The constructs' clattering becomes flapping, repeated when Illya speaks. This changes the sound of the scene without establishing a change to Caster's characterization.
RM-TD78-S1300-F026.explanation: The constructs' clattering becomes flapping, repeated when Illya speaks. This changes the sound of the scene without establishing a change to Caster's characterization.
RM-TD78-S1300-F026.sourceReading: The surrounding entities make a dry rattling or clattering sound and seem like hollow puppets; Illya identifies dragon-tooth golems.

RM-S05D-F033.description: A blood-vomiting image describing Caster's anguished laughter becomes an assertion that she actually coughs blood.
RM-S05D-F033.explanation: A blood-vomiting image describing Caster's anguished laughter becomes an assertion that she actually coughs blood.
RM-S05D-F033.sourceReading: Caster laughs as though vomiting blood, following her bitter response to the accusation that she killed Souichirou.

RM-S1303B-F015.description: The explanation changes an otherwise unavailable casting feat into something few mages could visualize. Caster's actual activation remains explicit, but the comparison establishing its exceptional nature is weakened.
RM-S1303B-F015.explanation: The explanation changes an otherwise unavailable casting feat into something few mages could visualize. Caster's actual activation remains explicit, but the comparison establishing its exceptional nature is weakened.
RM-S1303B-F015.sourceReading: Shirou says no mage could manifest this great magecraft with a single utterance, then allows advance preparation of a catalyst as a possible exception.

RM-R12B-F006.description: Caster's assurance that she has other resources becomes an assurance that she can control Saber, changing her stated reason for declining Kuzuki's protection.
RM-R12B-F006.explanation: Caster's assurance that she has other resources becomes an assurance that she can control Saber, changing her stated reason for declining Kuzuki's protection.
RM-R12B-F006.sourceReading: Caster says she has pieces available without borrowing Kuzuki's strength, answering his offer to guard her until Saber becomes usable.

RM-R12B-F016.description: The explanation loses Caster's wounded condition and the limitation of her magical defense. Her decision to shield Kuzuki with her body remains.
RM-R12B-F016.explanation: The explanation loses Caster's wounded condition and the limitation of her magical defense. Her decision to shield Kuzuki with her body remains.
RM-R12B-F016.sourceReading: The narrator conjectures that Caster recognizes her inability, in her wounded condition, to block the attack with her own magical power.

RM-R13B-F022.description: Caster's impending disappearance from exhaustion becomes something she is trying to accomplish, changing the agency of her desperate situation.
RM-R13B-F022.explanation: Caster's impending disappearance from exhaustion becomes something she is trying to accomplish, changing the agency of her desperate situation.
RM-R13B-F022.sourceReading: Caster is on the verge of disappearing alone because killing her Master has deprived her of sustaining magical energy.

RM-R13D-F015.description: Caster's promise to take very special care of Shirou becomes “treat you importantly,” losing the natural language of tenderness that sharpens her tool-making threat.
RM-R13D-F015.explanation: Caster's promise to take very special care of Shirou becomes “treat you importantly,” losing the natural language of tenderness that sharpens her tool-making threat.
RM-R13D-F015.sourceReading: Caster promises repeated, exaggerated care while threatening to turn Shirou into a tool, making apparent tenderness part of the menace.

RM-R6A-F011.description: Caster's continuing maintenance of living victims becomes a wish that they live. Her purpose of extracting all their magical energy remains explicit.
RM-R6A-F011.explanation: Caster's continuing maintenance of living victims becomes a wish that they live. Her purpose of extracting all their magical energy remains explicit.
RM-R6A-F011.sourceReading: Caster describes continually keeping people alive without killing them so that she can extract their energy to the last drop.

RM-R8A-F002.description: Issei's brother's enjoyment of calling Caster wicked becomes consideration of an evil identity, making his reported response more speculative and less amused.
RM-R8A-F002.explanation: Issei's brother's enjoyment of calling Caster wicked becomes consideration of an evil identity, making his reported response more speculative and less amused.
RM-R8A-F002.sourceReading: Issei reports that his brother delights in calling the guest a wicked woman, before giving his own favorable impression.

RM-R12A-F013.description: Caster's confidence that she can control a potential traitor becomes a need to prove her greatness to the world, adding an audience and changing her stated motive.
RM-R12A-F013.explanation: Caster's confidence that she can control a potential traitor becomes a need to prove her greatness to the world, adding an audience and changing her stated motive.
RM-R12A-F013.sourceReading: Caster says failure to control even Archer would expose her limited capacity, answering the risk that he might betray her.

RM-R10F-F007.description: The recollection drops both the hammer-like force of Kuzuki's blow and its impact on Rin's chest, leaving only an unspecified blow.
RM-R10F-F007.explanation: The recollection drops both the hammer-like force of Kuzuki's blow and its impact on Rin's chest, leaving only an unspecified blow.
RM-R10F-F007.sourceReading: Rin coughed after taking Kuzuki's hammer-like blow to her chest.

RM-R13A-F012.description: “Capture” specifies taking Kuzuki prisoner where the Japanese only requires overcoming him. This belongs in a dossier about combat objectives.
RM-R13A-F012.explanation: “Capture” specifies taking Kuzuki prisoner where the Japanese only requires overcoming him. This belongs in a dossier about combat objectives.
RM-R13A-F012.sourceReading: In all three branches, Rin says they need only overcome Kuzuki while Berserker handles the Servants.

RM-R14O-F001.description: “Grazed” replaces the snake's catching bite with passing contact. The passage still explicitly says Saber was seriously injured.
RM-R14O-F001.explanation: “Grazed” replaces the snake's catching bite with passing contact. The passage still explicitly says Saber was seriously injured.
RM-R14O-F001.sourceReading: Saber's narrow evasions allowed Kuzuki's changing attack to catch her like a biting snake.

RM-R9A-F007.description: Kuzuki's regret about insufficient ingenuity becomes regret about delivering too few blows, weakening his assessment of why his method failed.
RM-R9A-F007.explanation: Kuzuki's regret about insufficient ingenuity becomes regret about delivering too few blows, weakening his assessment of why his method failed.
RM-R9A-F007.sourceReading: Kuzuki says he should have used an additional trick or greater ingenuity, after recognizing that Saber will not fall for the same method twice.

RM-R04F-F009.description: Saber's assessment of breathing ideal for a human becomes breathing suited to Kuzuki's particular body, changing the standard of her praise.
RM-R04F-F009.explanation: Saber's assessment of breathing ideal for a human becomes breathing suited to Kuzuki's particular body, changing the standard of her praise.
RM-R04F-F009.sourceReading: Saber judges Kuzuki's breathing ideal by human standards, while restricting her admiration to breathing.

RM-P3-004.description: The English makes Kuzuki interrupt an almost finished exam and schedule its replacement for the next day. The Japanese specifies neither, making the disruption less precisely defined.
RM-P3-004.explanation: The English makes Kuzuki interrupt an almost finished exam and schedule its replacement for the next day. The Japanese specifies neither, making the disruption less precisely defined.
RM-P3-004.sourceReading: Students were vigorously filling in their answer sheets when Kuzuki canceled the exam and announced a retake on a later date.

RM-R14O-F005.description: The English makes the manner of Kuzuki's advance mysterious; the Japanese says Shirou does not even notice the advance itself.
RM-R14O-F005.explanation: The English makes the manner of Kuzuki's advance mysterious; the Japanese says Shirou does not even notice the advance itself.
RM-R14O-F005.sourceReading: Kuzuki closes the distance without Shirou even noticing his forward movement.

RM-R12A-F018.description: Kuzuki's effort to prevent either protagonist escaping becomes a shared intention to hold one another in place.
RM-R12A-F018.explanation: Kuzuki's effort to prevent either protagonist escaping becomes a shared intention to hold one another in place.
RM-R12A-F018.sourceReading: Kuzuki maintains the standoff to prevent either Shirou or Rin from escaping.

RM-R12B-F019.description: Caster's smile affirms that Kuzuki's very unresponsiveness suited her. The English makes her only perhaps content because of him, weakening that specific relationship.
RM-R12B-F019.explanation: Caster's smile affirms that Kuzuki's very unresponsiveness suited her. The English makes her only perhaps content because of him, weakening that specific relationship.
RM-R12B-F019.sourceReading: Caster corrects mere acceptance of Kuzuki's unresponsiveness: precisely his being that kind of person made him right for her.

RM-R14O-F002.description: The English repeats Shirou's inability to dodge instead of explaining that he cannot initiate a defense against fists he cannot see.
RM-R14O-F002.explanation: The English repeats Shirou's inability to dodge instead of explaining that he cannot initiate a defense against fists he cannot see.
RM-R14O-F002.sourceReading: Unable to see Kuzuki's fists, Shirou cannot initiate a defense himself; this follows a separate statement about his inability to evade narrowly.

RM-R9A-F008.description: The English turns a contrast between formless tactics and Kuzuki's recognizable method into secrecy, then replaces first-encounter lethality with a statement that the first strike must kill.
RM-R9A-F008.explanation: The English turns a contrast between formless tactics and Kuzuki's recognizable method into secrecy, then replaces first-encounter lethality with a statement that the first strike must kill.
RM-R9A-F008.sourceReading: The first anchor identifies absence of fixed form as tactical mastery. The second attributes lethality to first exposure, before the opponent understands Kuzuki's unusual form.

RM-R9B-F007.description: The English substitutes forearms for upper arms in the description of Kuzuki's changing attack.
RM-R9B-F007.explanation: The English substitutes forearms for upper arms in the description of Kuzuki's changing attack.
RM-R9B-F007.sourceReading: The narration identifies further changes in the upper arms after the initial lightning-fast movement.

RM-R12B-F024.description: A slight narrowing of Kuzuki's eyes becomes briefly closing them. The passage does not establish what emotion either gesture expresses.
RM-R12B-F024.explanation: A slight narrowing of Kuzuki's eyes becomes briefly closing them. The passage does not establish what emotion either gesture expresses.
RM-R12B-F024.sourceReading: Kuzuki slightly narrows his eyes before answering Shirou.

RM-R9A-F002.description: The English replaces the neck strike with the grip used for the subsequent throw, compressing two different actions.
RM-R9A-F002.explanation: The English replaces the neck strike with the grip used for the subsequent throw, compressing two different actions.
RM-R9A-F002.sourceReading: The narration recalls a neck strike followed by a remarkable throw; the next page separately describes gripping the neck during that throw.

RM-R14AA-F006.description: His refusal to allow objections becomes reluctance to make an offer. The surrounding threat and short reprieve remain.
RM-R14AA-F006.explanation: His refusal to allow objections becomes reluctance to make an offer. The surrounding threat and short reprieve remain.
RM-R14AA-F006.sourceReading: Gilgamesh ordinarily allows no objection or say in the matter; this time he grants a short reprieve.

RM-S1400B-F021.description: A slight widening of Gilgamesh's eyes becomes a moment of watching, removing his visible reaction before the laugh.
RM-S1400B-F021.explanation: A slight widening of Gilgamesh's eyes becomes a moment of watching, removing his visible reaction before the laugh.
RM-S1400B-F021.sourceReading: Gilgamesh slightly widens his eyes at Shirou's advance, then laughs with amusement before announcing his intention to kill him.

RM-S08D-F026.description: Kirei having kept Gilgamesh attached becomes Gilgamesh granting Kirei patronage, shifting the emphasis in their partnership.
RM-S08D-F026.explanation: Kirei having kept Gilgamesh attached becomes Gilgamesh granting Kirei patronage, shifting the emphasis in their partnership.
RM-S08D-F026.sourceReading: Gilgamesh credits their shared objective with Kirei having kept him attached thus far.

RM-S1512B-F002.description: Gilgamesh directly attributes his exposure to Saber. The English describes a spill without saying she caused it.
RM-S1512B-F002.explanation: Gilgamesh directly attributes his exposure to Saber. The English describes a spill without saying she caused it.
RM-S1512B-F002.sourceReading: Addressing Saber, Gilgamesh says this is what she showered him with ten years earlier.

RM-R14AB-F012.description: His ability to count the magic currently operating in Shirou becomes a broader claim about Shirou's magical capacity. The preceding count of seventeen remains.
RM-R14AB-F012.explanation: His ability to count the magic currently operating in Shirou becomes a broader claim about Shirou's magical capacity. The preceding count of seventeen remains.
RM-R14AB-F012.sourceReading: Gilgamesh says he can readily discern the number of spells operating in Shirou, explaining his preceding count of seventeen.

RM-R14AD-F009.description: Unexpected tenacity becomes something Gilgamesh says he already knew, reversing the expectation expressed in this line.
RM-R14AD-F009.explanation: Unexpected tenacity becomes something Gilgamesh says he already knew, reversing the expectation expressed in this line.
RM-R14AD-F009.sourceReading: Gilgamesh finds Shirou tougher to kill than expected after a blow he thought should have been fatal.

RM-R14F-F001.description: Rin's claim that equal numbers would balance their power becomes a possibility of challenging him. The next page still describes Emiya fighting on equal ground.
RM-R14F-F001.explanation: Rin's claim that equal numbers would balance their power becomes a possibility of challenging him. The next page still describes Emiya fighting on equal ground.
RM-R14F-F001.sourceReading: Rin says matching Gilgamesh's number of Noble Phantasms would balance their power.

RM-R14I-F003.description: Praise of Gilgamesh's capacity to hold and handle his arsenal becomes an overall 'greatest Heroic Spirit' ranking. The following limitation on his skill as a wielder remains.
RM-R14I-F003.explanation: Praise of Gilgamesh's capacity to hold and handle his arsenal becomes an overall 'greatest Heroic Spirit' ranking. The following limitation on his skill as a wielder remains.
RM-R14I-F003.sourceReading: The narration places Gilgamesh's capacity to possess and handle over a thousand Noble Phantasms at the summit among Heroic Spirits.

RM-R9C-F007.description: People he could do without become the least necessary people. His conclusion that none of the ten could be spared remains.
RM-R9C-F007.explanation: People he could do without become the least necessary people. His conclusion that none of the ten could be spared remains.
RM-R9C-F007.sourceReading: He sought to kill those among ten slaves whose absence would be acceptable, then found none expendable.

RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F006.description: Shirou asks about present visibility instead of what prompted Sakura's concern. Her explanation remains, and the change does not support this Gilgamesh dossier.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F006.explanation: Shirou asks about present visibility instead of what prompted Sakura's concern. Her explanation remains, and the change does not support this Gilgamesh dossier.
RM-FATE-D1-ESCORT-F006.sourceReading: Shirou asks whether something happened, and Sakura explains her recent sightings.

RM-HF-D4A-F003.description: Shirou's muscles locking when the man stands becomes admiration of firm, strong movement. Shirou still freezes later as the hand approaches his neck.
RM-HF-D4A-F003.explanation: Shirou's muscles locking when the man stands becomes admiration of firm, strong movement. Shirou still freezes later as the hand approaches his neck.
RM-HF-D4A-F003.sourceReading: The man's act of standing instantly makes Shirou's muscles lock. The following approach provokes an expectation of being killed.

RM-S12F-F018.description: A warning about becoming adapted or integrated turns into a warning that something will take a liking to Sakura. The Japanese leaves the precise direction of that adaptation unstated.
RM-S12F-F018.explanation: A warning about becoming adapted or integrated turns into a warning that something will take a liking to Sakura. The Japanese leaves the precise direction of that adaptation unstated.
RM-S12F-F018.sourceReading: Gilgamesh warns that once adaptation or integration has occurred, Sakura will no longer be able even to die. The sentence leaves the subject of 馴染む unstated.

RM-S1307B-F010.description: Shirou's mild disagreement with Rin's romantic description becomes agreement. His stronger conclusion that Gilgamesh sees Saber as property remains explicit.
RM-S1307B-F010.explanation: Shirou's mild disagreement with Rin's romantic description becomes agreement. His stronger conclusion that Gilgamesh sees Saber as property remains explicit.
RM-S1307B-F010.sourceReading: Shirou finds Rin's description slightly off, accepts that Gilgamesh is fixated on Saber, then sharpens that into treating her as property.

RM-S1307B-F027.description: His specific refusal to give his name becomes a broader refusal to address Caster. The contempt remains, while the withholding of identity becomes less explicit.
RM-S1307B-F027.explanation: His specific refusal to give his name becomes a broader refusal to address Caster. The contempt remains, while the withholding of identity becomes less explicit.
RM-S1307B-F027.sourceReading: Gilgamesh refuses to give his name to someone he deems a mongrel, then orders Caster away.

RM-S1400B-F024.description: The image of killing everything in sight becomes general murderous rage. His silent departure and its unexplained motive remain.
RM-S1400B-F024.explanation: The image of killing everything in sight becomes general murderous rage. His silent departure and its unexplained motive remain.
RM-S1400B-F024.sourceReading: His murderous aura suggests he would be satisfied only by killing everything in sight, yet he silently leaves.

RM-P3-023.description: Rin's acknowledgment that her wish also matters to her Servant becomes a denial that it concerns him. This reverses her initial understanding of Archer's condition for serving her.
RM-P3-023.explanation: Rin's acknowledgment that her wish also matters to her Servant becomes a denial that it concerns him. This reverses her initial understanding of Archer's condition for serving her.
RM-P3-023.sourceReading: Rin realizes that a Master's wish also concerns the Servant, then wonders why her having no wish should trouble Archer when he has his own.

RM-R04C-F007.description: Saber's assignment of rear support becomes an instruction to stay out of danger. The English preserves her objection to Shirou entering combat but drops the supporting work she assigns him.
RM-R04C-F007.explanation: Saber's assignment of rear support becomes an instruction to stay out of danger. The English preserves her objection to Shirou entering combat but drops the supporting work she assigns him.
RM-R04C-F007.sourceReading: Saber assigns the Master exclusively to rear support while claiming direct combat as her responsibility.

RM-S0401B-F007.description: The summoning changes from ordinarily impossible to unreasonable. The explanation that Servants respond to pursue their own wishes remains intact, so this belongs with the technical wording rather than this dossier's authority claim.
RM-S0401B-F007.explanation: The summoning changes from ordinarily impossible to unreasonable. The explanation that Servants respond to pursue their own wishes remains intact, so this belongs with the technical wording rather than this dossier's authority claim.
RM-S0401B-F007.sourceReading: Their desires explain their response to a summoning that would ordinarily be impossible or inconceivable.

RM-R14W-F009.description: An ability possessed by few Masters becomes an ability possessed by none. This makes dependence on the Grail categorical where Gilgamesh's explanation allows exceptional Masters.
RM-R14W-F009.explanation: An ability possessed by few Masters becomes an ability possessed by none. This makes dependence on the Grail categorical where Gilgamesh's explanation allows exceptional Masters.
RM-R14W-F009.sourceReading: Few Masters can sustain a Servant without Grail assistance; Gilgamesh's own anchor lacked the necessary energy.

RM-R3B-F010.description: Shirou's hypothesis that another mage controls Lancer becomes a hypothesis that Lancer and other Servants are familiars. The link from his attacker to a rival mage is no longer the stated basis of his deduction.
RM-R3B-F010.explanation: Shirou's hypothesis that another mage controls Lancer becomes a hypothesis that Lancer and other Servants are familiars. The link from his attacker to a rival mage is no longer the stated basis of his deduction.
RM-R3B-F010.sourceReading: Shirou hypothesizes that Lancer, too, is another mage's familiar and infers that he has entered a conflict between mages.

RM-S0408B-F001.description: Magecraft that summons Heroic Spirits and puts them into service becomes magecraft created from them. Shirou's question about Saber's identity still works, but his definition drops the act of employing a summoned spirit.
RM-S0408B-F001.explanation: Magecraft that summons Heroic Spirits and puts them into service becomes magecraft created from them. Shirou's question about Saber's identity still works, but his definition drops the act of employing a summoned spirit.
RM-S0408B-F001.sourceReading: Shirou understands the Servant system as magecraft that summons Heroic Spirits and employs them in service.

RM-S15G-F011.description: Rider's departure without returning to Sakura becomes an inability to return to her Master. The English supplies a constraint where the passage reports her course of action.
RM-S15G-F011.explanation: Rider's departure without returning to Sakura becomes an inability to return to her Master. The English supplies a constraint where the passage reports her course of action.
RM-S15G-F011.sourceReading: Rider departs to fight alone, neither returning to Sakura nor relying on Shirou's group, after rejecting his proposed means of saving her.

RM-HF-D14B-F020.description: Sakura is called a host with the reading 'Master' in Japanese; English retains only 'host.' The local pairing of receptacle and contractual role is lost, although a contract is mentioned shortly afterward.
RM-HF-D14B-F020.explanation: Sakura is called a host with the reading 'Master' in Japanese; English retains only 'host.' The local pairing of receptacle and contractual role is lost, although a contract is mentioned shortly afterward.
RM-HF-D14B-F020.sourceReading: The written 'host' is paired with the reading 'Master,' placing Sakura's receptacle role alongside a contractual designation as power passes to her.

RM-R14W-F011.description: Saber's comparison of the Masters' methods becomes a question about whether they were the same person. Gilgamesh's following answer concerns taking energy from others, which fits the Japanese comparison.
RM-R14W-F011.explanation: Saber's comparison of the Masters' methods becomes a question about whether they were the same person. Gilgamesh's following answer concerns taking energy from others, which fits the Japanese comparison.
RM-R14W-F011.sourceReading: Saber begins comparing Gilgamesh's Master with Rider's Master; the reply supplies the relevant similarity, taking energy from others.

RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F010.description: Archer's warning that this choice may cost lives becomes a categorical prediction that Shirou's choices will kill many people.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F010.explanation: Archer's warning that this choice may cost lives becomes a categorical prediction that Shirou's choices will kill many people.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F010.sourceReading: Archer warns that Shirou's chosen course may also result in many deaths.

RM-R04K-F007.description: The Japanese identifies the weapon as the mystery Rin cannot solve. English additionally says that she has not discovered Archer's identity.
RM-R04K-F007.explanation: The Japanese identifies the weapon as the mystery Rin cannot solve. English additionally says that she has not discovered Archer's identity.
RM-R04K-F007.sourceReading: The second 正体 specifies the first: Rin does not know the identity of the powerful Noble Phantasm fired as an arrow.

RM-S12D-F015.description: Temporary memory impairment becomes the loss of a fleeting memory fragment. This belongs with Shirou's threatened loss of self.
RM-S12D-F015.explanation: Temporary memory impairment becomes the loss of a fleeting memory fragment. This belongs with Shirou's threatened loss of self.
RM-S12D-F015.sourceReading: Using the arm will cause more than the temporary memory impairment Shirou experienced earlier.

RM-R14T-F017.description: English confines his hatred to his former self. Japanese also explicitly directs it at the people whose repeated predation disillusioned him.
RM-R14T-F017.explanation: English confines his hatred to his former self. Japanese also explicitly directs it at the people whose repeated predation disillusioned him.
RM-R14T-F017.sourceReading: His hatred has two objects: people who repeatedly take from each other and his former self who valued them.

RM-R2-014.description: The recollection of memories disappearing becomes a direct image of people dying, removing the source's emphasis on remembered life.
RM-R2-014.explanation: The recollection of memories disappearing becomes a direct image of people dying, removing the source's emphasis on remembered life.
RM-R2-014.sourceReading: The passage evokes memories disappearing without justification or meaning as it recalls the origin of the ideal.

RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F011.description: Archer's warning about confronting one's own inadequacy becomes a specific accusation of narrow-mindedness.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F011.explanation: Archer's warning about confronting one's own inadequacy becomes a specific accusation of narrow-mindedness.
RM-FATE-D7-ARCHER-SABER-F011.sourceReading: Archer anticipates Shirou confronting his own smallness or inadequacy, in a discussion of how little people can accomplish.

RM-LE-003.description: The English makes purposelessness sound like the reason his journey continued. This belongs with the traveler's purpose and longing, outside this dossier.
RM-LE-003.explanation: The English makes purposelessness sound like the reason his journey continued. This belongs with the traveler's purpose and longing, outside this dossier.
RM-LE-003.sourceReading: The journey continued because he had not found what he sought, rather than because he lacked a purpose.

RM-S1100-F008.description: Shirou privately infers arrow shooting where Japanese says bow drawing. That blurs the distinction between what he knows and his deliberately provocative complaint.
RM-S1100-F008.explanation: Shirou privately infers arrow shooting where Japanese says bow drawing. That blurs the distinction between what he knows and his deliberately provocative complaint.
RM-S1100-F008.sourceReading: Shirou infers that Archer has been drawing his bow; the following exchange establishes that he already knows no arrows were used.

RM-S1106-F003.description: Evidence of a severed neck becomes a large wound. The supplied passage does not establish an Archer-specific consequence.
RM-S1106-F003.explanation: Evidence of a severed neck becomes a large wound. The supplied passage does not establish an Archer-specific consequence.
RM-S1106-F003.sourceReading: Berserker's neck bears evidence of having been severed.

RM-S1117-F010.description: Archer's advice to confront his own mental image becomes a broader struggle against his mind. The preceding instruction to imagine his strongest self survives.
RM-S1117-F010.explanation: Archer's advice to confront his own mental image becomes a broader struggle against his mind. The preceding instruction to imagine his strongest self survives.
RM-S1117-F010.sourceReading: Archer identifies Shirou's own mental image as his opponent, following the instruction to imagine his strongest self.

RM-HF-DOJO-D14A-F028.description: Acquiring the key becomes unlocking the gate. This concerns the ritual's predicted progression and belongs outside this character dossier.
RM-HF-DOJO-D14A-F028.explanation: Acquiring the key becomes unlocking the gate. This concerns the ritual's predicted progression and belongs outside this character dossier.
RM-HF-DOJO-D14A-F028.sourceReading: Zouken predicts taking Archer's soul from the girl and seizing the key that leads to the gate.
